entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Break the militant Blackstone faction, recover sacred/civic material, and decide how the reclaimed temple will be used.
Religious leaders and residents ask the party to recover Blackstone Temple from a militant faction using the site as a fortified base.
The outcome changes which religious and civic factions trust the party.
{@b Leads onward.} Recovered supply records point toward Kellan’s Well, where armed crews from supposedly separate factions are using the same signals and supply marks.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Stop the temple leadership, rescue captives/recover relics, prevent desecration or a ritual.
{@b Player agency.} The party can assault, infiltrate, seek clerical support, or split rank-and-file followers from leaders.
{@b Fail forward.} Critical religious/history clues are automatic when the relevant shrine or records are examined.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Ignore large permanent-item piles. Across the entire chapter, keep legitimately portable valuables near {@b 300–400 gp}; the balance of the chapter’s monetary reward comes from the 500 gp civic/temple payment in the Rewards section. Also award 2 {@b Potions of Healing}, one appropriate 1st–3rd-level spell scroll, and one party-use uncommon item tied to the recovered relics.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Session 2 Opening — Return to Ledger House
entries: {@b Target runtime:} about 4 hours. Begin in late afternoon with the party immediately outside Ledger House after returning from the Slums. End after the party has entered Blackstone Temple and reached or clearly discovered the captives near the vestry.

entries.name: Scene A: Jord's Horse and Strongbox
entries: Jord is a traveling merchant preparing to establish a shop in Bellweather and is known to Brakkus. The party still has both his recovered horse and strongbox when the session begins.

If the horse and strongbox are returned, Jord pays {@b 50 gp to each character}, honors his promised future merchant discount, and gives the party {@b 2 Potions of Healing} in gratitude for recovering the horse.

The strongbox's wax seal is already broken. Jord can tell that someone opened it but cannot determine who. The actual sequence is that Blackstone kidnappers opportunistically stole and opened the box, then abandoned it in the dye house after encountering the spiders while moving through the district with the captured surveyors. Do not accuse the party without additional evidence.

If the characters stole anything from the box, Jord can notice missing inventory but still cannot know whether the party or the original thieves took it. Let their explanation and behavior shape his trust and future discount rather than producing automatic proof.

entries.name: Scene B: Ledger House Evening
entries: Play this scene broadly and let the players enjoy character interaction. Arumen naturally takes over the kitchen; Brakkus treats this as normal and is pleased to have them cooking.

Brakkus currently likes Arumen, believes Aaron is an ordinary human after Aaron's earlier explanation, is cautious with Jarrock because Jarrock has challenged his hostility toward 'Day Walkers,' and is broadly indifferent toward Pepper.

Brakkus has been asking patrons about Pepper's Library of Alexandria out of curiosity. He has heard rumors of an old library somewhere deeper in Bellweather's ruins, but he has no reliable location and should not imply that the Library of Alexandria itself is in Bellweather.

At a natural lull, Brakkus notices the official mark on Pepper's survey satchel and asks where it came from. He recognizes it as Council survey equipment because the crew worked openly out of Bellweather before disappearing. If Pepper says she found it abandoned in the Slums and no surveyors were nearby, Brakkus may reasonably theorize that the crew dropped it while fleeing or that someone took them, but he has no basis for naming a culprit or connecting them to Blackstone.

If another character tells Brakkus that Pepper deliberately killed Kaleb while he was unconscious, Brakkus takes the marked survey satchel from Pepper as evidence. He treats the killing as a serious unresolved matter but does not let it derail the immediate Blackstone rescue: innocent captives are in danger now. Brakkus makes clear that Pepper will answer for Kaleb's death after the urgent rescue is resolved.

{@b NPC description — Brakkus Ledgerhelm.} A powerfully built half-orc around forty-eight, with weathered green-gray skin, close-cropped dark hair touched with gray, and the posture of someone who spent decades wearing armor. At Ledger House he dresses simply, keeps his voice low, and rarely needs to raise it to control a room.

The paper still pinned to Ledger House's door is the completed Slums contract. The Council still believes its three-person survey crew disappeared while working in the Slums; the party has returned too recently for a thorough Council search to have happened. Brakkus has heard that the crew is still missing, but neither he nor the Council has connected their disappearance to Blackstone.

entries.name: Scene C: Bishop Brann's Petition
entries: After Brakkus has raised the subject, Bishop Brann arrives or is sent for. Preserve the existing Blackstone petition: armed occupiers have detained temple caretakers, Brann wants them alive, and he wants sacred records preserved.

{@b NPC description — Bishop Brann.} An elderly dwarf, short even by dwarven standards and broad around the middle, with deeply lined brown skin and a long silver beard divided into two neat braids. His well-kept clerical vestments have been repaired repeatedly at the cuffs and hem. He speaks slowly and deliberately, with the calm authority of someone accustomed to being listened to without raising his voice, and tends to frame problems in terms of who will suffer if the wrong choice is made.

Do not add the missing surveyors to Brann's Blackstone objective. At this point the Council still thinks the survey crew vanished in the Slums. Brann's request is separate: armed occupiers at Blackstone have detained temple caretakers, and he wants the caretakers rescued and the sacred records preserved.

Brann does not know what happened to Kaleb. If Pepper's satchel becomes part of the conversation, Brann recognizes it as Council survey equipment but does not have evidence of murder. Let player choices determine whether suspicion grows.
Derren's existing relic-recovery interest remains in canon. He can be mentioned here or held for the next Blackstone session if the opening is already busy.

{@b NPC description — Derren.} A small gnome priest with neatly trimmed hair, soot-darkened traveling hems, and a satchel crowded with notes, wrappings, and bits of devotional cord. He becomes noticeably more animated when discussing old relics or temple history.

entries.name: Scene D: Night and Morning Departure
entries: Allow planning, shopping that is reasonably available, and a long rest. The party leaves for Blackstone the next morning.
Do not push Aaron's Ledger House dream connection. If Aaron again investigates the building or says it feels familiar, allow another opportunity to connect Ledger House to the dreams.
Do not advance Arumen's unexplained teleportation yet. Mara remains out of sight this session.

entries.name: Scene E: Blackstone Reconnaissance
entries: Use the chapter's three established approaches: front court, broken side wall, or flooded drainage channel. Nearby residents know the watch changes every two hours and that food is being carried to captives near the vestry.
Let reconnaissance determine the first obstacle. Good planning can avoid a fight; failed or noisy approaches should create pressure rather than automatically trigger the chapter's full force.
The first clear information goal is simple: confirm that prisoners are alive and identify a route toward the vestry.

entries.name: Scene F: Level-3 Blackstone Pressure
entries: The party is intentionally still level 3. Do not run every level-4/5 encounter at full strength. Use one meaningful encounter, with a second only if the party is moving quickly and remains healthy.

For Tal Rusk's outer-line encounter, begin with {@b Tal Rusk and 2 Guards}. A third Guard can appear only if the alarm is raised or the party is dominating the fight. Tal challenges, bargains, withdraws, or surrenders when appropriate; his people are not suicidal.

If the party infiltrates through the side wall or drainage route, replace the frontal battle with a smaller patrol, stealth complication, or social challenge. Success should earn position and information, not merely remove hit points.
Keep the chapter's civilian distinction explicit. Nearby dependents, coerced refugees, and ordinary residents are not enemy combatants.

entries.name: Session 2 End Beat
entries: Aim to finish after the characters have entered the temple and reached, seen, or clearly located the captives near the vestry. Among the captives are Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin, two members of the survey crew the Council still believes vanished in the Slums. Their presence here is the first evidence available to the party that Blackstone was involved in the disappearance.

If Pepper still has Kaleb's marked satchel, a strong cliffhanger is for one rescued or visible surveyor to recognize it and ask, in substance, 'That's Kaleb's bag. Where is he?' If Brakkus has already taken the satchel after learning of Kaleb's murder, use the surveyors' presence itself as the reveal and let their questions about Kaleb create the tension instead.

Do not resolve Mason or the full liberation of Blackstone unless the players move dramatically faster than expected. The temple's decisive confrontation is intended to remain for the following session.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: When the Council or local clergy are ready to move against Blackstone Temple, {@b Derren} (gnome priest; use the {@creature Priest|XMM} stat block) approaches the party to recover relics held inside.

entries.name: Area Description
entries: The temple is a sturdy stone basilica that once served another faith. Bane's followers have covered the old plaster with black banners, crude devotional reliefs, and military slogans. Nearby houses hold faction members, dependents, refugees under coercion, and residents trying to survive under the faction's authority. Species never determines allegiance, and civilians are not combatants.

entries.name: Patrols
entries: Patrols exist to raise alarms, question strangers, and protect the perimeter. Use {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}, {@b Cultists}, and at most one {@creature Veteran|XMM} per patrol. A patrol that is clearly outmatched withdraws and alerts the temple rather than fighting to the death. Holy symbols, forged orders, disguises, bribery, or information from neighborhood residents can help the party bypass them.

entries.name: Mason's House
entries: Mason keeps a residence beside the temple. His guards are loyal but not suicidal. If the party attacks openly, Mason attempts to escape through a prepared back route and becomes a recurring problem. If the party infiltrates successfully, they can recover ledgers showing payments to recruiters, protection demands on nearby residents, and correspondence hinting at broader coordination among Bellweather's hostile factions.

{@b Treasure.} Mason’s house contains about {@b 300 gp} of the chapter’s 300–400 gp portable-valuable budget, plus two useful consumables and one story-relevant relic tied to the temple’s former faith. Do not add a second 750 gp cache.

entries.name: The Temple Interior
entries: The temple is lightly occupied during ordinary hours and more crowded during rites. The party can create an opening by disrupting a ceremony, turning a lieutenant, cutting off reinforcements, or entering through a service route.

Three hidden caches survive beneath old floor tiles. Important caches are found automatically once the characters have the correct records, a cooperative insider, or enough time to search; checks determine speed and complications rather than whether the adventure stalls. Together they contain:

items: two level-appropriate spell scrolls from the Cleric, Paladin, or Wizard lists;
two healing or utility consumables;
one uncommon magic item suited to the party;
historical records showing that Bellweather's enemies were being coordinated before the city's fall.

entries.name: Final Confrontation
entries: Run an objective-based confrontation with {@b Mason} (use {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}), one {@creature Veteran|XMM} enforcer, 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}, and 4 {@b Cultists}. If the party is fresh and the fight needs pressure, 2 {@b Berserkers} arrive after 2 rounds. The party can win by defeating Mason, breaking the faction's symbol of authority, recovering the relics, turning enough followers against him, or forcing a retreat.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Petition
entries: Bishop Brann asks for help recovering Blackstone Temple after armed occupiers seize the site and detain caretakers.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Brann wants the captives alive and sacred records preserved. Wern warns that the upper masonry is unstable. Perrin supports clearing the site because it blocks a useful route.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Bishop Brann is firm that surrendering enemies become prisoners, not trophies.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The militants have been removing records rather than burning them.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party chooses whether to approach openly, scout first, or seek a covert entrance.

The Council has no Blackstone objective involving the survey crew yet. From the Council's perspective, all three surveyors are still missing from the Slums. The party's discovery of Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin inside Blackstone is the first evidence linking their disappearance to the faction there.

entries.name: Scene 2: Reconnaissance
entries: Three approaches are available: front court, broken side wall, or flooded drainage channel.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Nearby residents know the watch changes every two hours and food is carried to captives near the vestry.
The drainage route is cramped but avoids the front sentries.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: No courier is expected today, giving the party a limited window before outside forces notice trouble.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Good reconnaissance can avoid one combat entirely.

entries.name: Scene 3: Outer Court
entries: The defenders challenge strangers before attacking.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A plausible cover story begins as social interaction. Obvious infiltration triggers combat.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Tal Rusk|NCFA}, believes he is holding the temple until “the Boss” secures the district. He does not know the Boss’s identity.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: For the current level-3 party, use Tal Rusk and 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}; a third Guard joins only if the alarm is raised or the party is clearly dominating. Tal and surviving defenders retreat inside when badly pressed rather than fighting to the death. At level 4 or higher, the DM can restore the original four-Guard pressure.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Tal carries a rotation note using the same crossed-line supply symbol seen in the Slums.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing Tal gives the party information about the vestry and sanctuary.

entries.name: Scene 4: Captives in the Vestry
entries: Several caretakers, one wounded guard, and the two surviving members of Kaleb's survey crew are confined near the vestry.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Freeing them removes the hostage threat from the final confrontation. One caretaker knows a maintenance passage behind the altar.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: The eldest caretaker, Nela Orr, a human woman, refuses to leave until the others are safe.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Nela overheard the leader order temple records packed for removal, suggesting someone wants information rather than destruction.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the captives remain imprisoned, the ritual leader later threatens them.

If Pepper still carries Kaleb's marked satchel, one of the surveyors recognizes it and immediately asks what happened to him. If Brakkus has already taken the satchel, Lessa and Kav still ask whether the party saw Kaleb in the Slums. The surveyors do not know Kaleb is dead. Their presence at Blackstone is the party's first proof that the missing crew was abducted.

entries.name: Scene 5: Sanctuary Ritual
entries: The leader is forcing captured records and relics into a coercive oath ceremony meant to bind the occupiers together.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: At initiative count 20, a brazier tips or masonry falls in a marked 10-foot area. Creatures there make DC 13 Dexterity saves or take 2d6 fire or bludgeoning damage. A character can use an action to stabilize one hazard permanently.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}, 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}, plus surviving outer defenders.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Written orders say “hold the black stone until the eastern route is secured” and are signed only “Boss.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the leader escapes, the documents still survive. If the documents burn, Tal or a captive can reproduce the key information.

entries.name: Scene 6: Who Controls the Temple?
entries: After the fighting, clergy, Council officials, and nearby residents all want a say in the site’s future.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Clergy want restoration. The Council wants a defensible civic post. Residents want shelter space. The party can advocate for one use or a compromise.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Record the recommendation for faction reputation. Advance to level 5 if using milestones.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 5
entries: Recovered supply records point toward Kellan’s Well, where armed crews from supposedly separate factions are using the same signals and supply marks.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} The Council and temple interests together provide {@b 500 gp} for breaking the extortion network and securing actionable evidence. Place another {@b 300–400 gp} in legitimately portable valuables across the temple and Mason’s residence, for a chapter cash/value target of about {@b 800–900 gp}. Also award 2 Potions of Healing, one 2nd-level Cleric/Paladin scroll, and one uncommon party-use item (default: {@b Driftglobe}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 350–500 gp in contract pay and recoverable valuables.
{@b Consumables.} 2 Potions of Healing and 1 spell scroll of 1st–3rd level.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item tied to the temple or recovered relics.
{@b Story reward.} Temple influence, stewardship credit, or a clerical favor.

entries.name: Session 2 Level-3 Combat Balance
entries: {@b Party baseline.} Balance Blackstone for four level-3 characters: Arumen, Aaron Dunamus, Jarrock, and Pepper. The party remains level 3 until Blackstone is resolved.

{@b Front Court.} Use {@creature Tal Rusk|NCFA} and 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}. A third Guard is optional reinforcement only if the party is clearly overwhelming the encounter. Tal tries to hold the entrance and raise the alarm; he does not need to fight to the death.
{@b Broken Side Wall.} Use 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} and 2 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}. Good stealth, deception, distraction, or another strong plan can bypass this fight entirely.
{@b Flooded Drainage Channel.} No automatic combat. Use environmental complications first. If the party makes enough noise or otherwise alerts the occupants, use 1–2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

{@b Optional Interior Response.} Only if the party is moving quickly or has raised an alarm, use 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} and 1 {@creature Scout|XMM}. Do not add another Veteran-class enemy before the captive rescue.
{@b Encounter principle.} Avoid replacing a successfully bypassed encounter with an unrelated combat. Clever infiltration should reduce the number of fights.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Control Kellan’s Well, prove that separate crews answer to a higher command, and open a useful underground route.
Separate armed crews have begun using the same patrol signals around Kellan’s Well, suggesting coordination beyond ordinary criminal activity.
The evidence is the first strong indication that someone is organizing threats across multiple districts.
{@b Leads onward.} Merchants and workers affected by protection rackets confirm that Koven House is the network’s payment and storage center.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Control access to the well, recover evidence, prevent escape or reinforcement.
{@b Player agency.} Negotiate with captives or lower-ranking members, scout tunnels, or attack openly.
{@b Fail forward.} If stealth fails, enemies become prepared; the route and core evidence remain accessible.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Kellan's Well sits in a ruined district where several armed groups have recently begun using the same signals and patrol routes. The Council wants to know whether the cooperation is temporary, criminal, or connected to the Boss.

entries.name: 1. Well Chamber
entries: The shaft opens into a stone chamber used as a checkpoint. A small mixed patrol challenges intruders. Use {@creature Goblin Warrior|XMM|Goblins}, {@creature Orc|XMM|Orcs}, {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits}, or equivalent stat blocks in a four-to-six-creature encounter appropriate to the party. They attempt to raise an alarm and fall back rather than fight to the death.

entries.name: 2. Bow Gallery
entries: A side chamber overlooks the approach. Archers use cover and withdraw after one or two volleys if pressured. A shallow floor depression is an old maintenance pit, not a species-sensitive trap; its cracked edge and loose stones make it detectable before anyone falls.

entries.name: 3. Junction
entries: This room connects multiple routes and contains chalk marks showing a shared command system. Characters who stop to examine them automatically learn that different groups are using the same schedule and symbols.

entries.name: 4. Barracks
entries: Off-duty fighters rest here. Their personal effects include letters, ration chits, and pay tokens from more than one faction. Captured or persuaded occupants know that {@b Noren Vale} coordinates the local crews on behalf of someone higher up.

entries.name: 5. Command Room
entries: {@b Noren Vale} is a pragmatic local commander represented by a {@creature Veteran|XMM} or {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM}. He is loyal to Tyren because Tyren provides weapons, money, and protection, not because of ancestry or supernatural compulsion. Noren retreats if defeat becomes likely and can become a recurring source of information if captured or convinced to cooperate.

entries.name: 6–8. Escape Routes and Stores
entries: The remaining chambers contain supplies, a hidden exit, and a small reserve of tribute waiting to be moved deeper into Old Bellweather. Use about {@b 400–500 gp} in mixed valuables here, two consumables, and documents stamped with Tyren’s seal. This cache is part of the chapter’s 1,000–1,100 gp monetary target; do not add the source adventure’s enormous hoard.

entries.name: Tactical Response
entries: If the alarm is raised, the defenders try to hold a junction while Noren evacuates the documents. They do not create an unavoidable pincer or infinite reinforcement loop. The party can break contact, negotiate, or pursue.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The chapter succeeds when the party obtains clear evidence that the Boss is coordinating otherwise separate groups. Capturing Noren, seizing the correspondence, or turning one of the crews all provide that evidence. The catacombs also become a useful emergency route into the ruined city.

entries.name: Scene 1: Briefing and Objectives
entries: Kellan’s Well appears to be a simple occupied strongpoint, but the real objective is evidence of coordination.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Secure the entrance. Prevent runners from warning deeper forces. Recover correspondence or supply records.
If the party captured anyone at Blackstone Temple, a prisoner can provide the first password.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The Council knows different crews use identical hand signals around the well but does not know who directs them.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party can accept a Council contract or investigate independently.

entries.name: Scene 2: Well Chamber
entries: The visible well house covers stairs into old waterworks.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: One scout tries to flee down the stairs on round 2 unless stopped.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 3 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} and 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Crates carry the same crossed-line mark. A chalk schedule identifies crews by color instead of faction.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If a runner escapes, deeper defenders are prepared; otherwise the party can surprise the next area.

entries.name: Scene 3: Bow Gallery
entries: Archers control a flooded passage from behind broken masonry.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can advance under cover, climb a maintenance ledge, or use the water channel. A far-side lever releases stored water; creatures in the channel make DC 14 Strength saves or fall prone and move 15 feet.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Bypassing rather than killing the archers preserves potential prisoners.

entries.name: Scene 4: Barracks and Prisoner
entries: Mixed equipment from several factions is stored together, along with a prisoner who refused new orders.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Rask, an orc mercenary, was jailed for refusing to attack civilians. Freeing him provides an independent witness.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Rask is suspicious but practical. He says different bands receive instructions from the same masked courier.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A supply ledger lists Koven House and Paden Square as delivery points.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Fair treatment earns Rask’s testimony later.

entries.name: Scene 5: Command Junction
entries: The local commander attempts to burn the message cache when alarmed.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: At the end of round 1, the commander ignites the papers unless a character reaches the desk or uses an action to extinguish them.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 3 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Surviving pages order rival groups to avoid fighting each other while Bellweather remains the priority. A map marks Koven House as a supply and payment center.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the cache burns, Rask and the supply ledger still point to Koven House; the campaign does not stall.

entries.name: Scene 6: Return and Reaction
entries: The evidence proves that Bellweather faces an organized network rather than unrelated gangs.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Wern treats the problem as military coordination. Bishop Brann worries about civilians in occupied areas. Perrin recommends cutting the supply network first.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Brakkus remarks that someone who can make enemies cooperate is more dangerous than any one gang.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Koven House becomes the next logical target.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 6
entries: Merchants and workers affected by protection rackets confirm that Koven House is the network’s payment and storage center.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Reopening the route and recovering the command evidence earns {@b 600 gp} from civic and merchant interests. Place another {@b 400–500 gp} in mixed coin, valuables, and hostile-faction stores, for about {@b 1,000–1,100 gp} of total monetary value. Also award 2 useful consumables and the documents bearing the Boss’s seal.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 300–450 gp in salvage, gems, and civic pay.
{@b Consumables.} 2 general consumables plus 1 exploration-focused consumable.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item recovered from the wellworks.
{@b Story reward.} Improved water access or infrastructure and goodwill from workers who benefit from the reclamation.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Dismantle the Koven House criminal network and recover evidence connecting stolen reclamation goods to buyers in the city.
Stolen reclamation goods and protection rackets lead the characters to Koven House, headquarters of a criminal network profiting from Bellweather’s expansion.
Breaking the network reduces street crime but creates a political problem: some of the people implicated are useful to Bellweather’s recovery.
{@b Leads onward.} Bellweather authorizes an expedition to Savin Keep to secure the harbor approach and investigate the “old watch.”

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Reach the command room, seize ledgers, free prisoners, force surrender, or break the network.
{@b Player agency.} Stake out the house, infiltrate, recruit an informant, enter through service routes, or assault.
{@b Fail forward.} A triggered trap costs position, time, or resources; essential evidence survives somewhere in the house.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Keep the chapter’s immediately spendable or saleable value near {@b 1,500 gp total}. Divide that value between unclaimed tribute, coin, gems, legitimate salvage, and any civic recovery payment; do not count identifiable stolen property twice. The party also keeps {@b one +1 weapon}, {@b one +1 shield}, 2 useful spell scrolls of 3rd level or lower, and 2 consumables. Remove the pile of multiple +1 weapons, +2 shield, high-level scrolls, and oversized gem haul.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use {@creature Scout|XMM}, {@creature Spy|XMM}, {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM}, {@creature Thug|XMM}, and at most one {@creature Master Thief|XMM}-style high-tier opponent. Replace the repeated automatic backstabs with hidden movement, readied ambushes, traps, and retreat routes. The mansion should feel like fighting a prepared thieves' guild, not enduring unavoidable damage.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Koven House becomes relevant once organized theft and extortion begin spilling into reclaimed streets. The Council can post the job, but victims, merchants, or neighborhood residents can also point the party toward the house.

entries.name: Area Description
entries: The mansion and the surrounding yard are in excellent condition. The litter and dilapidation so common elsewhere in Bellweather is not present here. The outer yard (area 1) and the central courtyard (area 6) are open to the sky. All other areas are roofed.

entries.name: Encounter 1: Outer Yard
entries: The outer yard is deserted. Nothing happens here.

entries.name: Encounter 2: Auxiliary Buildings
entries: Areas 2, 3, and 4 were once a groundskeeper's cottage, kennel, and hound master's quarters. The old kennel is now occupied by {@b Perris}, a quickling who wants privacy and has no loyalty to the criminal cell. Perris warns respectful characters that the mansion is trapped and can identify one concealed service entrance. A small gift or simply agreeing to leave Perris alone is enough; no bribe is required. If threatened, Perris flees rather than fighting.

entries.name: Encounter 3: The Mansion
entries: The mansion is divided between {@b ambush routes} (rooms 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, and 24) and {@b hazard rooms} (11, 12, 14, 19, 22, and 23). Rooms 5 and 6 are useful breathing spaces. These labels describe how the criminal cell prepared the house; they do not mean an ambush or trap automatically triggers on entry. Ambushers use secret routes, cover, the Hide action, and coordinated retreats. Hazards use the {@b Interactive Trap Replacements} above and always provide a tell, a countermeasure, and normal 2024 resolution.

The first time the characters enter a trapped room, use the {@b Interactive Trap Replacements} above. Do not use the automatic-hit traps, percentage detection, reset-on-return assumptions, or instant or opaque poison effects. Criminals know the safe routes and can deliberately lure intruders toward hazards, but a trap should always have a visible tell, a way to mitigate it, and consequences short of arbitrary character removal.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Use the {@b Treasure Override} for this chapter. The house still contains stolen furnishings, art, coin, documents, and contraband, but most of it belongs to identifiable victims or is too bulky to function as adventuring treasure. Recovering and returning stolen property can improve Civic Trust or Merchant Standing. Keep at most one memorable permanent magic item from the source hoard; convert the rest to consumables, evidence, or valuables held for restitution.

entries.name: Scene 1: Finding the Network
entries: Koven House functions as a criminal headquarters, warehouse, and prison.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Victims identify wagon schedules and known lookouts. A former runner can sketch the yard in exchange for immunity from minor theft charges.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Stolen reclamation supplies have been routed through the property for months.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Preparation can reveal the cellar entrance before combat.

entries.name: Scene 2: Outer Yard
entries: Lookouts supervise wagons and hired muscle.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Capturing the yard quietly grants advantage on the party’s first stealth or deception check inside the mansion.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}. The scouts run for the mansion if fighting begins.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the alarm is raised, the leaders start destroying records.

entries.name: Scene 3: Workshops and Coerced Workers
entries: Auxiliary buildings contain stolen goods and laborers forced to repair equipment.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Freeing workers reveals a hidden cellar entrance. A weighted shelf trap can be spotted with DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) and disabled with DC 14 Dexterity using thieves’ tools.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Workers know prisoners are kept below the mansion.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Saving workers provides witnesses for later prosecutions.

entries.name: Scene 4: Mansion Leadership
entries: Vara Koven directs the network from the upper floor while Dorn holds the main stair.

{@b NPC description — Vara Koven and Dorn.} Vara is a tall tiefling woman in early middle age, slim and sharply dressed for a criminal hiding place, with swept-back horns, controlled movements, immaculate gloves, and the practiced smile of someone who prefers deals to bloodshed. Dorn is a heavyset human man in his forties, scarred, plainly armed, and watches the stair rather than the conversation; his expression suggests he would rather settle the matter with steel.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Vara bargains if escape seems unlikely. Dorn prefers combat.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Vara Koven|NCFA} uses the Bandit Captain stat block. {@creature Dorn|NCFA} uses the Warrior Veteran stat block.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Vara, Dorn, 3 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}. Vara attempts to flee through the rear office at half hit points.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Ledgers name legitimate merchants who knowingly bought stolen goods. Payments from an unknown patron funded guards to keep Bellweather out of deeper districts. A note warns, “Island remains sealed. Do not disturb the old watch until ordered,” referring to Savin Keep.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing Vara alive makes later testimony easier but is not required.

entries.name: Scene 5: Cellar Prison
entries: Two merchants, a city guard, and a clerk who refused to falsify shipping documents are held below.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The clerk can authenticate the ledgers.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: The clerk is frightened of retaliation but testifies if the party promises protection.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The witnesses prevent implicated merchants from dismissing the evidence as fabricated.

entries.name: Scene 6: Public Fallout
entries: Back in Bellweather, arrests and arguments follow.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Some merchants cooperate and pay restitution. Others argue that the city cannot afford to destroy businesses over wartime compromises. Perrin publicly supports prosecution of clear criminals, increasing his credibility.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin should still appear principled here. His later betrayal works better if his earlier positions sometimes make sense.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The references to Savin Keep make the island fortress the next strategic objective.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 7
entries: Bellweather authorizes an expedition to Savin Keep to secure the harbor approach and investigate the “old watch.”

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Keep total immediately spendable or saleable value near {@b 1,500 gp}. About half can be coin, gems, and unclaimed tribute; the rest can be a civic recovery payment, restitution, or legitimate salvage. Identifiable stolen goods are returned to victims and earn favors rather than extra cash. Also award one +1 weapon, one +1 shield, 2 scrolls of 3rd level or lower, and 2 consumables.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} About 1,500 gp in portable criminal hoard. Bulky identifiable stolen goods are intended for restitution rather than liquidation.
{@b Consumables.} 2 consumables and 2 spell scrolls of 3rd level or lower.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item; add a second uncommon item only if the party missed an earlier permanent reward and is behind the campaign curve.
{@b Story reward.} Evidence, witnesses, restitution, and improved standing with merchants or workers harmed by the operation.

data.name: Chapter 7: Reconquest of Savin Keep
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 6–7

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/savin_keep.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/savin_keep.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Secure Savin Keep, free its bound defenders, and recover the first strong historical evidence of Tyren.
Bellweather needs Savin Keep to secure the harbor approach, but the ruined keep is still defended by undead bound to old orders.
Holding Savin Keep gives the city a strategic foothold and yields historical evidence naming Tyren as a force connected to Bellweather’s earlier fall.
{@b Leads onward.} The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Solve/bypass the undead defenses, break the binding, hold the keep during the counterattack.
{@b Player agency.} Research before departure, parley with bound spirits, use passwords, or force a military solution.
{@b Fail forward.} Passwords and historical clues have redundant sources. Missing one changes difficulty, not solvability.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Keep the {@item Potion of Heroism}, the hidden historical records, and either a {@item +1 Warhammer} or {@item +1 Shield}. Convert the remaining stockpile of permanent magic weapons into about {@b 700 gp} of legitimate salvage and ceremonial equipment; the Council separately pays 1,000 gp for reclaiming the keep.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Keep the undead premise. Use {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}, {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}, {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters}, and one {@creature Wight|XMM} as patrol leadership. Keep {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} where appropriate. Replace the mass counterattack with a tactical force such as a {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblins}, 2 {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, and 2 {@b Worgs}, adjusting counts to the party's current strength.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Savin Keep stands on an island guarding Bellweather's harbor approach. The Council waits until nearby waters and landing points are reasonably secure before authorizing the mission. The objective is not to exterminate everything on the island; it is to make the keep safe enough for a permanent garrison and recover whatever records survived the fall.

entries.name: Approach and Passwords
entries: Three fragments—{@b Lux}, {@b Shestnik}, and {@b Samosud}—appear on old notes and plaques around the keep. Characters can learn that they were challenge-and-response phrases used by the final defenders. Discovering any two makes the third easier to infer from Ferren Marten's records. The passwords let the party bypass some undead guardians, but they are not required to complete the chapter.

entries.name: 1. Outside the Gate
entries: A weathered skeleton lies among reeds and stones. Its equipment is ruined, but a corroded medallion and partial note preserve two password fragments. A careful search also reveals tracks from a recent hostile reconnaissance team.

entries.name: 2. Gate and Courtyard
entries: The wooden gate is barely functional. Inside, the courtyard is patrolled by a small group of {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} bound to the keep's final defense. Use one encounter appropriate to the party's level; the guardians ignore anyone who gives the correct password. Once combat begins, they fight until destroyed or the party withdraws beyond the gate.

entries.name: 3. Stable
entries: A collapsed stable contains an obvious patch of chemically damaged timber. Disturbing the rafters releases a {@creature Gray Ooze|XMM} or other corrosive creature or hazard appropriate to the party. The danger is telegraphed by dissolved nails and pitted stone.

entries.name: 4. Granary
entries: Pale fungus grows across old grain bins. A character proficient with Nature, Medicine, or an herbalism kit can identify a harmless restorative strain. Harvesting it yields one use that grants advantage on the next saving throw against the Frightened condition made before the next Long Rest.

entries.name: 5. Smithy
entries: The smithy is home to several territorial {@b Giant Frogs} or another small coastal predator. Behind the hearth lies a well-preserved weapon from the old garrison. Replace the original generic +1 weapon with one uncommon martial item appropriate to the party or with a named heirloom that can be returned to Bellweather for reputation.

entries.name: 6. Barracks
entries: The ruined barracks hold echoes of the final defenders. These manifestations do not attack. If greeted respectfully or with a password, they point out a hidden diary describing the unnatural coordination of the armies that destroyed Bellweather. This is an automatic clue to Tyren's historical influence.

entries.name: 7. Kitchen
entries: An {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} has spread through the ruined kitchen. A sour mineral odor, warped metal, and partially dissolved wood warn attentive characters. Roll Initiative normally if the party enters carelessly. The room contains salvage and one consumable reward after the creature is dealt with.

entries.name: 8. Entrance Hall — Counterattack
entries: When the party reaches the watchtower interior, a Tyren-aligned strike team lands on the island to prevent reclamation. Use a compact force such as one {@creature Veteran|XMM} commander, two {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, and four {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} or equivalent creatures. Their objective is to seize the gate and burn the surviving records, not to fight to the last creature. If the commander falls or half the force is defeated, the survivors withdraw toward their boats.
The undead guardians oppose the strike team as readily as they oppose the characters. Clever parties can exploit that conflict.

entries.name: 9. Armory
entries: Most racks are empty. An illusory wall conceals a surviving cache. Award one uncommon permanent item, one consumable, and mundane salvage rather than several stacking +1 items.

entries.name: 10. Officer's Quarters
entries: A nearly transparent predator—use an appropriate ooze, mimic-like creature, or {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM} only if the party's tier supports it—has made this room its hunting ground. Scratches and dragged dust provide warning. A parchment here contains the final password fragment.

entries.name: 11. Old Chapel
entries: The spirit of {@b Ferren Marten}, last chaplain of Savin Keep, appears near the altar. He is not inherently hostile. If the party identifies themselves as Bellweather's reclaimers and treats the dead with respect, Ferren explains that Bellweather fell because powerful leaders were unnaturally unified by a force associated with a radiant pool. He names {@b Tyren}, {@b Edra}, and {@b Toran}, and points the party toward records once kept at Marren Library.

Ferren then releases the remaining defender-spirits from their duty. If attacked, use a {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} chassis appropriate to the party, but the scene is intended as revelation rather than combat.

entries.name: Securing Savin Keep
entries: The mission succeeds when the party has broken the binding on the defenders, prevented the counterattack from destroying the site, and made the approach safe enough for a Council garrison. On return, shipping begins expanding almost immediately.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Crossing
entries: The party leads the first landing while a small Bellweather guard detachment waits offshore for a signal.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stealth or bad weather can conceal the boat. Bright light or loud magic alerts the gate.
Old signal bells begin ringing without visible hands as the party approaches.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The keep appears abandoned but reacts to intruders according to ancient routines.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: An undetected landing lets the party inspect the gate before combat.

entries.name: Scene 2: Gate and Courtyard
entries: Undead defenders continue commands issued during Bellweather’s last fall.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They hold assigned posts and do not pursue far beyond them.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}, 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A guardroom tablet says “hold until relieved by lawful command,” implying the binding can be ended.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Destroying every undead works, but learning the release phrase reduces later resistance.

entries.name: Scene 3: Barracks and Shrine
entries: A ruined shrine preserves the oath formula used by the last commander.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters who search the shrine find the release phrase and learn that speaking it at the command stone can end the old watch.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The oath names the last commander and confirms the undead were defenders, not invaders.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This discovery reframes the keep as a tragedy rather than a monster nest.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Stone
entries: The binding focus is defended by the last commander’s wight.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking the release phrase causes ordinary skeletons to stop fighting immediately.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Wight|XMM}, 4 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A sealed report names Tyren as a possessing force linked to disturbances around the Radiant Well generations ago.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This is the first historical evidence that the present “Boss” may be connected to an older threat.

entries.name: Scene 5: Counterattack
entries: Living Tyren-aligned troops attack before Bellweather can occupy the keep.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party must hold either the dock or gate for 5 rounds. At the end of round 5, Bellweather reinforcements arrive.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Holding the keep secures the harbor route and turns the site into a Bellweather garrison.

entries.name: Scene 6: Records of Ownership
entries: Old inventories recovered from the keep identify surviving archives tied to the Cardon family’s Weavehouse.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests access to the records and proposes reclaiming the Weavehouse next.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The records are genuine and establish a plausible Cardon claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 7 if using milestones.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 8
entries: The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Reclaiming Savin Keep earns a {@b 1,000 gp} civic/military payment plus about {@b 700 gp} in legitimate salvage and ceremonial equipment. Also award a Potion of Heroism and either a +1 Shield (default) or +1 Warhammer if the party needs a weapon. Historical records are evidence and civic leverage rather than saleable loot.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 600–900 gp in military salvage and Council bounty.
{@b Consumables.} 2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item. A thoroughly searched concealed armory can hold a second uncommon item only if the party is behind the campaign reward curve.
{@b Story reward.} A Council garrison, expanded shipping security, and access to a strategic base.

data.name: Chapter 8: Cardon Weavehouse
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 7–8

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/cardon_weavehouse.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/cardon_weavehouse.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Reclaim the Cardon Weavehouse and force the party to confront the difference between public risk and private inheritance.
Perrin Cardon asks the Council to reclaim his family’s old Weavehouse, presenting the mission as both civic recovery and restoration of lawful ownership.
Whatever the decision, Perrin recovers enough wealth and documentation to become a much more influential figure in Bellweather.
{@b Leads onward.} The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Secure the building, identify the real ownership/treasure question, survive rival claims.
{@b Player agency.} Honor Cardon’s claim, challenge it, negotiate public use, or bargain for concessions.
{@b Fail forward.} The Cardon history is discoverable through multiple records and witnesses.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Most recovered wealth belongs to the property itself or the Cardon claim. Let the party recover {@b 500–750 gp} in immediate valuables and one uncommon permanent item at most. The larger economic reward is Cardon's restored fortune and rising influence.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Favor current urban predators and occupiers: {@creature Ettercap|XMM} + {@b Giant Spiders}, {@b Wererats}, {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, {@b Veterans}, or another group that makes sense for the current district. Preserve the family's hidden-wealth story rather than any specific creature count.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Restored Wealth
entries: The Weavehouse is the turning point in Perrin's material power. He recovers enough wealth, documentation, and credit to hire protection, sponsor repairs, make loans, and reward political allies. Even if the party limits his property claim, he emerges from the chapter richer and more visible than before.
Do not present this as a secret coup. Residents should notice Cardon-funded work crews, guards, charitable gestures, and merchants suddenly taking his calls.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Council authorizes reclamation of the old Cardon property after the surrounding route is reasonably secure. Perrin publicly frames the mission as civic recovery, but privately wants proof of ownership and the family cache returned to him.

Before departure, Perrin offers {@b Taren Vale}, an aging household retainer represented by a {@creature Scout|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} as appropriate. Taren remembers the old layout imperfectly and can sketch the broad plan. His private instruction is to identify Cardon heirlooms and report what the party finds. He does not steal from the characters or force the outcome.

If the party recovers disputed property, Perrin first attempts a legal claim through the Council. The characters can accept compensation, challenge the claim with records, negotiate public use, or demand an independent hearing. The Council is institutionally inclined to protect documented ownership, but it is not predetermined to side with Perrin. Reputation, evidence, and witnesses matter.

entries.name: Occupying Warband
entries: A Tyren-aligned mixed warband currently controls the Weavehouse. Most members are gnolls, but species is not the faction's moral identity. The complex also contains dependents, injured people, coerced workers, and younger noncombatants. Those people flee, hide, or surrender if given a safe route.
The warband uses an alarm drum. Once raised, patrols consolidate around the courtyard, gates, and chief's hall rather than spawning endless reinforcements.

entries.name: 1. Outer Gates and Courtyard
entries: The old Cardon crest is still visible beneath the warband's angular red mark. During the day, one patrol watches the courtyard; at night, more off-duty members gather here around fires. The party can infiltrate over a wall, bluff at a gate, enter through collapsed structures, or trigger a direct fight.

entries.name: 2. Collapsed Wing
entries: Burned-out structures contain refuse, unstable flooring, and a corrosive ooze. The area also provides a concealed route around the main courtyard for characters willing to crawl through debris.

entries.name: 3. Watchpost
entries: A distracted three-person patrol watches one approach. Their duty roster contains Tyren's seal and references tribute demanded from multiple independent factions—useful evidence that the Boss is coordinating more than one group.

entries.name: 4–5. Former Servants' Quarters
entries: These rooms house junior guards and people low in the warband hierarchy. They are the easiest occupants to convince to stand down, especially if the party promises safe passage. One knows where prisoners and noncombatants are being kept.

entries.name: 6. Main Hall
entries: The warband leader uses this former reception hall as a command post. Use a gnoll leader if one fits the party's level; otherwise use a {@creature Gladiator|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} with gnoll appearance and a small escort. The leader's goal is to preserve control of the site and escape with Tyren's correspondence if defeat becomes likely.

entries.name: 7–9. Living Quarters
entries: These rooms contain dependents, wounded members, and off-duty retainers. Treat them as a social and moral complication, not an encounter quota. If the party indiscriminately attacks noncombatants, Neighborhoods & Workers and Independent Factions reputation suffer.

entries.name: 10. Garden
entries: The old kitchen garden has gone wild. A hidden cistern provides a quiet route between buildings and can serve as a defensible short-rest location once secured.

entries.name: 11. Cardon Bedroom and Cache
entries: The family cache is concealed behind old plaster. A ten-minute search finds it automatically; a successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds it immediately. The art objects are historically and legally significant, not merely loot. Their total market value is substantial, but the chapter's {@b Treasure Override} determines what portable wealth the party actually receives.
Finding the cache creates the chapter's central choice: return it to Perrin, place it in Council custody, use Marren Library records to challenge ownership, or negotiate a public settlement.

entries.name: 12. Shrine and Correspondence
entries: A spiritual leader represented by a {@creature Priest|XMM} or {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM} keeps Tyren's letters and tribute demands. The correspondence makes clear that the warband is being rewarded for obedience and threatened for independence. This is another automatic clue to the Boss's methods.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The site is reclaimed when the command structure is broken, civilians and dependents are no longer trapped inside, and the Council can occupy the property without immediate counterattack. What happens to the property itself is a political question, not a dungeon reward.

entries.name: Scene 1: Perrin’s Claim
entries: Perrin presents deeds showing that his family owned the Weavehouse before Bellweather fell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: He asks the party to secure the property and preserve surviving records. He does not ask them to harm current occupants.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin genuinely believes restored ownership will attract investment and stabilize Bellweather.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Workers warn that several families and a small armed band now use the complex.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party can seek relocation guarantees before entering.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Courtyard Occupants
entries: Civilian squatters live under the protection of a warband that charges them for food and safety.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking with civilians first identifies which structures contain fighters and which contain families.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Mara Pell, a halfling woman, speaks for the families and wants time plus guaranteed relocation. Korrin Vale leads the armed group and wants the stored goods.

{@b NPC description — Korrin Vale.} A broad, powerfully built dragonborn man in repaired military gear with no matching insignia left on it, Korrin has dark bronze scales, a chipped horn, and the bearing of a discharged soldier rather than a street tough. He keeps his weapons maintained, gives short orders, and becomes noticeably less certain when separated from his followers.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Residents know the records vault has remained sealed.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Treating civilians fairly earns durable neighborhood support.

entries.name: Scene 3: Armed Wing
entries: Korrin’s fighters hold the warehouse and counting room.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Korrin surrenders if isolated and reduced below half hit points. Civilians do not fight unless attacked.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA} uses the Warrior Veteran stat block.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated surrender prevents unnecessary civilian displacement.

entries.name: Scene 4: Records Vault
entries: The sealed vault contains deeds, payrolls, debt books, and customer inventories.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Separate the documents into Cardon property, worker property, customer consignments, and public historical records.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The building belongs to the Cardon family, but not everything inside does. Correspondence mentions scholars at Marren Library studying “radiant disturbances” before the fall.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party’s handling of the records establishes a precedent others later cite.

entries.name: Scene 5: The Settlement
entries: Perrin, residents, workers’ descendants, and Council clerks make competing claims after the danger is gone.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can advocate for strict deed ownership, compensation and relocation, shared recovery, or another arrangement.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin accepts a lawful compromise in public even if it limits his gain; he remembers who opposed him.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Perrin gains enough wealth and standing to become a major Council voice. Marren Library becomes the obvious next historical target.

entries.name: Optional Jarrock Thread: Rena Dask
entries: Rena Dask attends or sends a statement on behalf of reclamation crews. She does not claim the Cardon family has no rights; she argues that workers who took the physical risks of reopening the property should receive enforceable safety standards, compensation, or a defined public benefit rather than only wages and thanks.

If Jarrock supports her automatically, have Rena acknowledge a legitimate Cardon claim the evidence actually supports. If he dismisses her automatically, have her point to a concrete injury, unpaid cost, or public subsidy. Keep the question difficult rather than making either side a caricature.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 9
entries: The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} The Council, affected tenants, and commercial interests generate about {@b 2,000 gp} of total party value: roughly {@b 1,200 gp} in payment, restitution, or lawful recovery awards and {@b 800 gp} in immediately portable coin, jewelry, or uncontested valuables. Major property assets remain in legal process. Also award one uncommon item (default {@b Sending Stones}) found in the old office.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 500–750 gp in immediately portable valuables; the larger fortune is tied to ownership and property claims.
{@b Consumables.} 1–2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} At most 1 uncommon permanent item unless the party is substantially behind the campaign curve.
{@b Story reward.} Legal leverage over Perrin Cardon and the possibility of negotiated public-use concessions.

data.name: Chapter 9: Marren Library
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 8–9

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/marren_library.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/marren_library.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Recover Bellweather’s documentary memory and reveal Tyren as a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
Bellweather gains access to Marren Library, one of the best surviving collections of pre-fall records.
By the end of the chapter, the party should understand that Tyren is not merely a warlord but a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
{@b Leads onward.} With valuable districts reopening, old families and investors begin pressing claims in the Mansion District.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Preserve records, identify Radiant Well references, choose who receives copies.
{@b Player agency.} Work for Cardon, work for the Council, copy records independently, or involve scholars/temples.
{@b Fail forward.} Core Radiant Well clues are guaranteed; checks determine how complete and private the discovery is.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Knowledge is the reward. Give the party 2–4 useful spell scrolls appropriate to their level, one uncommon or rare utility item, and valuable manuscripts worth {@b 500 gp} if sold—or much more as leverage with scholars and the Council.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use constructs, undead scholars, and aberrant scavengers where the source calls for generic guardians: {@creature Animated Armor|XMM}, {@b Flying Sword}, {@creature Specter|XMM}, {@creature Ghoul|XMM}, {@creature Mimic|XMM}, {@b Gibbering Mouther}, or {@b Nothic}. Keep intelligent encounters conversational when possible.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Administrative Network
entries: Perrin uses wealth and archive access to cultivate clerks, recordkeepers, merchants, and junior officials. If the party gives him records, the network grows faster; if they resist, he builds it through copies, public filings, favors, and patronage.
He still does not control the Council, but he increasingly understands which forms, seals, schedules, and staff actually make Bellweather's government function.

entries.name: Marren Library Tactical Map Key
entries: The replacement Marren Library map is intentionally compact and table-buildable. Use the numbered areas below as the authoritative geography for Chapter 9. The Cardon Weavehouse map remains unchanged.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Marren Library is valuable because it contains the documentary memory Bellweather lost when the city fell. Perrin wants specific records concerning old property, the Radiant Well, and the Cardon family's claims. The Council publicly describes the mission as preservation.

entries.name: Entering the Library
entries: The building is damaged but recognizable. Collapsed walls create multiple entrances. The party's challenge is less about clearing every room than about finding the right collections while protecting fragile records from hazards and opportunists.

entries.name: 1. Entrance & Foyer
entries: The library’s main entrance is damaged but usable. A small reception desk, display cases, and scattered civic notices make the building’s former public function obvious. Characters who pause here can identify the safest routes into the reading room and offices without a check.

entries.name: 2. Reading Room
entries: This broad central room is the party’s primary research space. Long tables and open shelves create clear lanes of movement and plentiful half-cover. Searching here reveals catalog references pointing toward the Librarian’s Office, Reference Alcove, General Stacks, and Restricted Stacks.

entries.name: 3. Librarian’s Office
entries: The head librarian’s office contains administrative ledgers, accession lists, property correspondence, and notes connecting several pre-fall researchers to the Radiant Well. A meaningful search automatically identifies which collections contain the campaign’s essential historical clues.

entries.name: 4. Study Room
entries: A quiet group-study chamber with a large table and wall shelving. Independent scholars, scavengers, or another intelligent faction can be encountered here. Treat this as a social-first scene: cooperation can produce catalog information, while threats or violence risk damage to nearby records.

entries.name: 5. Reference Alcove
entries: Rare and frequently consulted works are kept here. One {@creature Animated Armor|XMM} and two {@creature Flying Sword|XMM} guardians protect the sealed reference cases. They activate only when someone forces a case or removes protected material without satisfying the library’s old authorization mechanism.

entries.name: 6. General Stacks
entries: The largest surviving collection fills tightly spaced rows. A {@creature Basilisk|XMM} has nested among damaged shelves; toppled cases and narrow aisles create cover and movement choices. The party can bypass it by using the Reading Room and Reference Alcove routes rather than treating the stacks as a mandatory fight.

entries.name: 7. Scribe Room
entries: Copying desks, inks, blank folios, and preservation supplies remain usable. Once the party finds important records, this room lets them make controlled copies before deciding who receives originals. Ten minutes of careful work produces a serviceable duplicate of one discovered document set.

entries.name: 8. Restricted Stacks
entries: The locked restricted collection contains the strongest Radiant Well and possession material. A {@creature Specter|XMM} tied to the old library serves as a social-first guardian and attacks only if the collection is threatened or deliberately destroyed. The essential revelations here are automatic: Tyren can survive by transferring between hosts, and the Radiant Well can admit or alter consciousness. The pre-fall “no cause for alarm” Council circular is also stored here.

entries.name: 9. Storage
entries: Supply crates, book carts, damaged archival boxes, and wrapped salvage fill this small room. One suspicious container can be a {@creature Mimic|XMM} if an extra encounter is useful; otherwise this area holds preservation materials and the chapter’s utility-item reward rather than another compulsory fight.

entries.name: 4–6. Reading Rooms and Entrance Hall
entries: These areas contain rotted furniture, faded murals, and scattered fragments. They are useful for quiet exploration and for foreshadowing the institution Bellweather once was rather than for mandatory combat.

entries.name: 8–11. Workrooms and Carrels
entries: Most supplies are ruined, but careful salvage can recover a modest amount of gold leaf, inks, vellum, and tools. Use these as crafting materials or civic salvage rather than a large cash payout.

entries.name: The Historical Refrain
entries: Among pre-fall Council records is the circular quoted earlier in this chapter: {@b “There is no cause for alarm.”} It was issued while reports of coordinated hostile movement were already accumulating. This is the adventure's clearest historical echo of the title.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The party succeeds by securing the most important records and determining how they will be held. Giving everything to Perrin strengthens him. Putting the archive under Council or independent stewardship creates different political consequences. The essential Tyren clues are preserved regardless.

entries.name: Scene 1: Reaching the Library
entries: The library is structurally damaged and occupied by scavengers and magical hazards. The party’s objective is preservation as much as exploration.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A smoke plume from one wing means some records are already in danger. Characters can enter through the garden court, main hall, or a broken upper window.
Every hour spent without stabilizing the fire destroys one minor collection; this does not remove essential clues.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather scholars provide a list of three priority collections: civic annals, magical research, and property records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party must choose what to protect first, giving the expedition an immediate priority.

entries.name: Scene 2: Reading Room and Stacks
entries: The reading room opens into damaged stacks where old guardians and ruin predators can complicate the search.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Moving carefully reveals signs of recent human passage leading to the stacks.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles} if the party disturbs the central monument. They defend the courtyard only.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A satchel dropped by scavengers contains copied page numbers from the magical research wing. Someone else is looking for the same records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing or tracking the scavengers can reveal that they were paid anonymously.

entries.name: Scene 3: Stacks and Fire
entries: A collapsed lamp has started a spreading fire while frightened scavengers try to remove selected volumes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters can fight the fire, stop the scavengers, or split up. Three successful actions using water, magic, blankets, or DC 13 ability checks contain the fire.
The scavengers surrender if cornered; they were hired to recover specific research, not burn the building.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Their leader, Tessa Marr, was promised 200 gp by a masked intermediary and knows only a drop location.

{@b NPC description — Tessa Marr.} A rangy wood elf woman who looks young by elven standards, tall and narrow-built, with cropped auburn hair, a patched hooded coat, and the restless gaze of someone always measuring distance to the nearest exit. She carries herself like a scout rather than a bruiser and speaks quickly once she realizes a fight is going against her.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} if negotiation fails.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The requested volumes concern the Radiant Well, possession, and “personality transference.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Saving the stacks earns scholar and public goodwill.

entries.name: Scene 4: Master Librarian’s Chamber
entries: The locked chamber contains the most coherent pre-fall account of Tyren.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A damaged ward triggers when the desk is forced. DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or dispel magic suppresses it; otherwise each creature in the room makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The journal states that Tyren is an intelligence capable of occupying living hosts. The Radiant Well amplifies or facilitates the transfer. The author believed destroying a host would not necessarily destroy Tyren.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This changes the campaign’s central question from “Who is the Boss?” to “What intelligence is possessing the figure the factions call the Boss, and how does it move between hosts?”

entries.name: Scene 5: Property Archives
entries: The property wing contains deeds and debt records useful to Bellweather’s present-day disputes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests originals relating to Cardon holdings. Council clerks want all civic records retained publicly. Scholars want conservation before distribution.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin is especially attentive here but remains within legal procedure.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Several records show how emergency powers during Bellweather’s fall transferred public assets into private hands.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Who controls these records affects later property disputes and Perrin’s political leverage.

entries.name: Scene 6: Return and Publication
entries: The party must decide who receives originals, copies, and public access.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: At minimum, the Tyren material can be copied before any ownership dispute is settled.
Brakkus urges making dangerous historical information available to more than one institution.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Essential revelation: Tyren is a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Consequences
