entries: Advance to level 9 if using milestones. The next phase focuses on wealth and property returning to the city, beginning with the Mansions.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 10
entries: With valuable districts reopening, old families and investors begin pressing claims in the Mansion District.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} The recovery and preservation effort provides about {@b 2,400 gp} of total economic value: {@b 1,400 gp} in Council/scholarly payment and up to {@b 1,000 gp} in manuscripts, inks, and rare texts if sold. Keeping the manuscripts instead can create greater leverage with scholars and the Council. Also award 3 useful spell scrolls of levels 2–4 and one uncommon/rare utility item (default {@b Eyes of Minute Seeing}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 300–500 gp in recoverable valuables, rare books, and research grants.
{@b Consumables.} 2 spell scrolls and 1 utility consumable.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare utility or knowledge-focused item; use a strong uncommon item instead if the party is already ahead on rare gear.
{@b Story reward.} Research access and discoveries concerning Tyren, Bellweather, or the Radiant Well.

data.name: Chapter 10: The Mansions
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 8–9

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Resolve three property cases that establish how Bellweather treats inherited claims, current occupants, and public-use promises.
With major streets reopening, several families and investors ask the party to enter the old Mansion District and resolve competing claims.
Perrin uses the resulting legal climate to strengthen private ownership and his own political influence.
{@b Leads onward.} Reports from occupied territory describe a thriving illicit market in Paden Square where rival factions trade under a shared truce.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Recover heirlooms, expose false claims, protect residents, decide what is public/private salvage.
{@b Player agency.} Accept private commissions, demand public terms, mediate rival heirs, or prioritize public safety.
{@b Fail forward.} Documents needed to adjudicate a featured claim are always recoverable with investigation.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Table-Ready Use
entries: Treat the Mansion District as a flexible set of 1–2 session commissions from old families, investors, displaced descendants, and opportunists. Each commission should expose a different argument about ownership. Use the source map as a reusable neighborhood rather than clearing every building.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use the current party tier and the organized-town encounter guidance. Private employers may accompany the party, creating protection and social complications. Keep family claims and hidden vaults central.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Committee Authority
entries: After the Mansion precedents are set, Perrin is elevated to chair Bellweather's {@b Reclamation and Emergency Works Committee} or its local equivalent. The office gives him legitimate access to contracts, requisitions, seals, property hearings, and administrative staff.
The appointment is public and defensible: Perrin has money, experience, and a record of supporting reclamation. This is the institutional bridge that makes his later abuse of procedure plausible.

entries.name: Optional Jarrock Thread: Rena's Challenge
entries: Use Rena Dask once during the Mansion property cases if Jarrock has engaged with her earlier. She asks him to explain the principle behind his decisions: inherited title, current occupation, labor invested, public need, or some combination.
Rena should challenge inconsistency, not demand a predetermined political answer. After this scene, let the subplot recede unless Jarrock actively keeps the relationship alive.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Mansion District was once home to Bellweather's richest families. Decades of abandonment, occupation, looting, and fire have left most properties damaged, but old vaults, legal records, heirlooms, and sealed rooms make the district newly valuable as reclamation reaches the river.

The Council has no single military objective here. Instead, the party receives competing commissions from descendants, current residents, investors, neighborhood advocates, and civic officials. The point of the chapter is not to clear every mansion. Run {@b three featured property cases}, each presenting a different question about ownership.

entries.name: Featured Case A — The Vell House
entries: {@b Claim.} Mara Vell, a descendant with credible records, wants family portraits and a sealed deed box recovered.
{@b Complication.} Two families have been living in the service wing for six years and have repaired part of the property.
{@b Opposition.} 2 {@b Gargoyles} and 2 {@b Animated Armors} remain bound to the old house.
{@b Choice.} Recover the heirlooms without displacing the residents; negotiate a tenancy; or turn the entire claim over to a Council hearing.

entries.name: Featured Case B — The Doran Vault
entries: {@b Claim.} Two distant heirs present conflicting documents.
{@b Complication.} A professional recovery crew led by a {@creature Veteran|XMM} has already entered under a private contract.
{@b Opposition.} A {@creature Mimic|XMM}, unstable floors, and the rival crew if negotiations fail.

{@b Evidence.} The vault contains a notarized codicil showing that part of the estate was gifted to a public hospice before Bellweather fell. This evidence is found automatically if the vault is opened.

entries.name: Featured Case C — The Harroway Garden
entries: {@b Claim.} An investor wants the property cleared for redevelopment.
{@b Complication.} A small community of squatters has converted the surviving courtyard into homes and workshops.
{@b Opposition.} A territorial {@creature Shambling Mound|XMM} in the overgrown conservatory is the actual danger. The residents are not enemies.
{@b Choice.} Clear only the monster and leave the civic dispute to negotiation, support the investor's claim, or advocate for a new use agreement.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The chapter is complete after the party resolves three substantial property cases or otherwise establishes a precedent that changes how Bellweather handles reclaimed estates. Their choices determine which factions gain reputation and how later residents talk about the party.

entries.name: Structure of the Chapter
entries: Run the Mansion District as three separate cases. Each mixes physical danger with a property dispute. The party can resolve them in any order.

entries.name: Case A: The Vell House
entries: A legitimate heir, Sera Vell, asks the party to clear her family home, which is occupied by dangerous creatures and a caretaker family that has lived there for years.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Clear the unsafe upper floor, then determine what happens to the caretakers.
Sera has valid title and is not cruel; the caretakers have nowhere else to go.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Sera, a human woman, wants her home back but agrees to reasonable relocation terms. The caretaker, Old Ren, an elderly dwarf, distrusts promises made by officials.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Ettercap|XMM|Ettercaps} and 3 {@creature Giant Spider|XMM|Giant Spiders} in the sealed upper rooms.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The house records show the Vells paid city taxes even after evacuation, strengthening the legal claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated tenancy or relocation earns goodwill from both sides. Immediate eviction helps strict property advocates but harms residents.

entries.name: Case B: The Doran Vault
entries: A wealthy claimant named Joric Doran presents documents claiming a sealed townhouse and its vault.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The deed is convincing at first glance. Inside, the party encounters traps and an old household guardian.
A careful search reveals the claim papers are altered copies.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Joric is charming, impatient, and offers the party a private bonus to “avoid delays.”

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM} as the old vault guardian. It attacks anyone lacking the original family signet.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The true deed names a different family whose surviving descendants are poor laborers in Bellweather. DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) spots inconsistencies in Joric’s papers even before the original is found.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Exposing the fraud embarrasses several officials who endorsed Joric. Accepting his claim gives Perrin ammunition to argue that private verification should replace public review.

entries.name: Case C: Harroway Garden
entries: A once-grand estate is now home to dozens of squatters and a productive community garden.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The danger comes from a buried cistern contaminated by an {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. Clearing it makes the property far more valuable.
Afterward, investors offer to buy the claim from a distant heir who has never visited Bellweather.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Community leader Nessa Harroway, a half-orc woman, is not related to the old owners; she took the name from the district. She wants legal recognition for current residents.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. The fight takes place around narrow cistern walkways; falling into the sewage imposes the Poisoned condition until the creature takes a short rest and washes.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The old estate records contain no surviving direct heir, only a chain of speculative claims.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Supporting current occupants creates a precedent for use-based claims. Supporting investors creates a precedent favoring documented ownership and capital.

entries.name: District Resolution
entries: Once all three cases are resolved, the Council debates what precedents they establish.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin argues for predictable ownership rules. Bishop Brann argues that reclamation should not create homelessness. Wern, a dwarf, cares mainly that disputes do not destabilize security.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin cites the party’s own decisions selectively, whichever ones support his position.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: These legal precedents matter later when Perrin uses institutional authority against the characters.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 11
entries: Reports from occupied territory describe a thriving illicit market in Paden Square where rival factions trade under a shared truce.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Across the chapter, keep direct payments, lawful salvage, restitution, and saleable art near {@b 2,500 gp total}; do not pay the maximum separately for every case without regard to that chapter cap. A typical resolved case is worth 600–900 gp in cash, valuables, or equivalent favor. Limit the chapter to one rare item total, default {@b Ring of Protection} from a voluntarily surrendered heirloom claim only if the party resolves the public-use dispute fairly; otherwise replace the item with 750 gp in art/coin within the same chapter budget.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 1,000–1,500 gp total in portable coin, art, jewelry, and salvage.
{@b Consumables.} 2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item. Add an uncommon item only if the party missed earlier major rewards.
{@b Story reward.} Property claims, allies, and additional political pressure on Cardon interests.

data.name: Chapter 11: Paden Square
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 9–10

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/paden_square.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/paden_square.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Infiltrate or turn Paden Square, identify Tyren’s agents, and prove Tyren coordinates trade as well as military force.
Scouts learn that Paden Square has become a functioning market inside occupied territory and that representatives of several hostile factions trade there.
The recovered correspondence proves that Bellweather is facing an organized strategic enemy rather than unrelated gangs.
{@b Leads onward.} The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Control exits, protect civilians, seize command correspondence, or convince part of the force to defect.
{@b Player agency.} Direct assault, infiltration, staged trade, sabotage, or faction negotiation.
{@b Fail forward.} Command evidence is not lost because one courier escapes; another source remains.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: After the party brings back evidence that supposedly separate hostile groups are coordinating, an official Council statement describes the activity as {@b "localized resistance"} and says there is {@b "no cause for alarm within Reclaimed Bellweather."} The statement may be technically true—the walls are still holding—but it minimizes what the characters have actually learned.
If the party brings the notice to Ledger House, Brakkus can read the final sentence and reply, {@b "Well. That settles it, then."} He immediately starts checking the shutters and cellar stores.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Present the plaza as a functioning hostile market rather than a room-by-room extermination. Social infiltration, bargaining, disguise, and violence should all work.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Paden Square was once Bellweather's commercial heart and remains a trading nexus inside occupied territory. The Council learns that a supposedly powerful magic item will be auctioned there and that Tyren may send a representative.

entries.name: Entering the Square
entries: Paden Square is busy, commercially active, and occupied by people from many factions and species. The party can enter as merchants, hired guards, couriers, bidders, entertainers, laborers, or invited guests. Cover depends on credentials and behavior, not ancestry.

If the characters' cover is weak, use a group Charisma (Deception) check against DC 14. On a failure, security questions them, demands a sponsor, or escorts them away; combat is only one possible consequence.

entries.name: Security and Scale
entries: The square is too crowded and fortified for a sensible direct assault, but do not represent that with hundreds of combatants. A frontal attack triggers escalating security, civilian panic, blocked exits, and a clear need to withdraw. Use one immediate security encounter and then a chase or escape procedure.

entries.name: Scene 1: Mission and Cover
entries: Paden Square is an active market inside hostile territory. The objective is intelligence, not extermination.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can enter disguised as buyers, escort a cooperating merchant, sneak across rooftops, or stage a diversion.
Their goals are to identify who enforces the truce, learn what Tyren's network is purchasing, and seize correspondence if possible.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather knows representatives of several hostile factions attend the same market without fighting.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A violent entrance causes vendors and couriers to scatter, making intelligence harder to recover.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Market
entries: Run the square as a social environment before combat.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Merchants sell weapons, food, medicine, stolen civic goods, and information. Many are criminals, but some are ordinary people trading because official routes are closed.
The party can gather three pieces of intelligence through conversation, observation, bribery, or theft.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin, a goblin broker, is talkative and self-protective. Balden, a human enforcer, speaks for the market’s security committee. Neither is automatically hostile.

{@b NPC description — Garin and Balden.} Garin is a small, neatly dressed goblin man of indeterminate middle age with ink-stained fingertips, bright rings, and the constant half-smile of a broker who expects every conversation to become a transaction. Balden is a tall, heavyset human man in his thirties, shaved-headed and watchful in reinforced street clothes, standing just far enough back to let Garin do the talking until trouble begins.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The “Boss” buys maps, old records, alchemical reagents, and captives with unusual magical exposure.
Couriers use the crossed-line mark and carry sealed packets toward Storen Gate.
The market truce is enforced by threats from a central command, not mutual trust.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Good social play can complete most objectives without combat.

entries.name: Scene 3: The Auction
entries: A private auction offers an old civic map, captured correspondence, and a magical research folio.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can bid, steal, expose a seller, or disrupt the auction.
If they win or seize the correspondence, it names Storen Gate as the primary logistics route.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin will quietly help the party if convinced Bellweather can keep the market open under safer rules later.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If combat starts, use 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, and 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}. Civilians flee rather than fight.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The correspondence refers to the central commander only as “Boss,” but includes orders to move forces through Storen Gate and references “the host” in singular terms.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing documents is more important than defeating every enemy.

entries.name: Scene 4: Escape or Negotiated Exit
entries: Once the party’s purpose is exposed, exits begin to close.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They can escape through alleys, bargain with Garin, create a crowd panic, or fight a delaying action.
Use a three-success chase if needed: Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, or clever magic.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A captured courier can confirm that orders ultimately come from Varen Keep.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the party is captured, market leaders prefer ransom or trade to execution; allies can create a second chance.

entries.name: Scene 5: Bellweather Learns the Scale
entries: The evidence proves the hostile network has logistics, markets, couriers, and strategic command.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Wern proposes taking Storen Gate to cut the supply route. Perrin supports the plan because it would open valuable interior districts.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 10 if using milestones.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 12
entries: The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays {@b 2,000 gp} for reliable intelligence on the command network and another {@b 2,000 gp} if the party secures the auctioned material for civic custody, for a maximum cash reward of {@b 4,000 gp}. Material sold back to lawful owners should create favors or restitution rather than duplicate the payout.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} About 1,000 gp in seized payroll, trade goods, and bounty or reward money.
{@b Consumables.} 2–3 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item or equivalent party-use item.
{@b Story reward.} Disruption of the hostile intelligence network and improved access toward Storen Gate.

data.name: Chapter 12: Storen Gate
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 10–11

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/storen_gate.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/storen_gate.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Take Storen Gate as a strategic objective and open the safest land route into deeper ruins.
Storen Gate blocks the safest land route into the deeper ruins and allows Tyren-aligned forces to move troops without interference.
Capturing Storen Gate opens the city’s deeper districts and shifts the campaign from local reclamation to open strategic conflict.
{@b Leads onward.} With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Open/hold the gate, prevent a signal, defeat or turn the command element.
{@b Player agency.} Climb, infiltrate, bribe an insider, create a diversion, or conduct a frontal attack.
{@b Fail forward.} Failure to stop a signal adds reinforcements or pressure rather than ending the scenario.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Treat this as a military objective. Success is measured by controlling the alarm, gate mechanism, command post, and reinforcement timing rather than by defeating every defender.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Emergency Authority
entries: Opening Storen Gate turns reclamation into a larger security and trade problem. Perrin's committee authority expands into emergency contracting, public notices, and coordination with merchants and guards. He is now the Council's dominant administrative voice even when other councilors disagree with him.
Wern still controls military judgment and Bishop Brann still carries moral/public influence; Perrin's power comes from procedure, money, records, and the ability to make government move.

entries.name: The Wall
entries: Characters approaching openly are warned away from the wall and directed to the gate. Characters climbing, flying, or sneaking across contend with watch rotations, cover, and magical observation. Resolve the approach with the normal 2024 stealth, perception, and spell rules rather than percentage detection.

entries.name: The Gate
entries: Merchant wagons still pass through under permit, which gives the party several options:

items: buy or borrow a legitimate wagon and paperwork;
forge a permit or impersonate a supply crew;
hide among cargo and make a group Dexterity (Stealth) check against the guards' passive Perception;
bribe a corrupt clerk;
create a distraction elsewhere on the wall;
attack directly.

entries: Failure does not mean instant combat. Guards question the party, demand inspection, separate one character for verification, or call an officer. Combat begins only if the situation escalates there.

entries.name: Capturing the Gate
entries: The gate can be secured by defeating the command group, convincing enough troops to stand down, or disabling the portcullis and signal system long enough for Bellweather's forces to arrive. Once the defenders' command collapses, rank-and-file troops may retreat or surrender.

entries.name: Scene 1: Planning the Assault
entries: Storen Gate is a military objective with four goals: silence the alarm, open the gate, seize the command post, and hold it.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can choose stealth, climbing, sabotage, infiltration with captured signals, or direct assault.
Bellweather troops wait out of sight until the gate opens or a signal is given.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Scouts identify the alarm tower, gate mechanism, barracks, and command post on the keyed map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Each objective completed before open combat reduces enemy reinforcements.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Wall
entries: Sentries control the outer wall and alarm bell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: If the bell rings, add one additional group of defenders to the gate encounter after 2 rounds.
Cutting the bell rope, jamming the clapper, or silently removing the sentries prevents the reinforcement.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A signal chart shows Paden Square, Storen Gate, and Varen Keep on the same command network.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Silencing the alarm gives the party control over the pace of the assault.

entries.name: Scene 3: Gate Mechanism
entries: The mechanism room is defended because the enemy expects Bellweather to want the gate intact.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A character at the controls can open the gate with an action after the locking bar is removed. Removing it requires DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or two uninterrupted actions with tools.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Opening the gate brings Bellweather troops into the battle at the start of the next round.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Post
entries: The local commander tries to destroy orders and retreat toward the inner city.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stop the commander, seize documents, or pursue if necessary.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Commander Vesk|NCFA} uses the Hobgoblin Captain stat block and values survival over martyrdom.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 3 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Orders refer to Tyren directly for the first time in contemporary documents and instruct commanders to “protect the host.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A living Vesk can confirm Tyren is not physically present at every command site.

entries.name: Scene 5: Hold the Gate
entries: The party must hold the command position until Bellweather forces secure both approaches.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Run 4 rounds of pressure rather than a mass battle. Each round presents one threat: archers, a breach, a retreating squad, or fire near the mechanism. Let the party choose where to intervene.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use small groups of {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors} or {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}; do not place dozens of creatures on the map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Success opens the deeper city and marks the transition from reclamation to open war.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 13
entries: With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays {@b 5,000 gp total} for opening and holding Storen Gate, reflecting the strategic importance of the objective. Captured military supplies become Council property rather than additional resale loot. Also provide one rare consumable or utility reward (default {@b Potion of Speed}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 1,250–1,750 gp in Council military reward and captured command valuables.
{@b Consumables.} 3 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item from the command post or armory.
{@b Story reward.} Gate access, garrison support, and reopening of a major trade route.

data.name: Chapter 13: Valen Cemetery
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 11–12

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/valen_cemetery.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} End the escalating undead crisis, rescue abducted people, and reclaim Bellweather’s cemetery as a civic place for the dead.
Reports that began as disturbed graves have escalated into disappearances and organized undead attacks around Valen Cemetery.
Reclaiming the cemetery restores a civic place of mourning and removes one of the most visible signs that Bellweather’s recovery is failing.

After the cemetery crisis is resolved, reports of worsening contamination in the Storen River become independently urgent. Following the poisoned water leads toward Maren Isle; Hessa's records are not required and do not connect her to Yaren.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Protect the living, disrupt undead creation, identify and defeat the controlling threat.
{@b Player agency.} Research, holy support, stealth, daylight timing, or direct cleansing.
{@b Fail forward.} Lore needed to understand the source is given through graves, clergy, and survivors; checks add weaknesses/shortcuts.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Build the escalation from {@b Skeleton/Zombie} to {@b Ghoul/Ghast}, {@creature Wight|XMM}, {@creature Wraith|XMM}, {@creature Specter|XMM}, and finally the vampire or vampire-spellcaster equivalent appropriate to the party's level. Undead should arrive in distinct scenes rather than one giant attrition swarm.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Independent Threat: Hessa Vale
entries: Hessa Vale is not a servant of Tyren and does not work for Yaren. She is exploiting Bellweather's instability for her own necromantic ambitions. Valen Cemetery deliberately demonstrates that the campaign world contains dangerous actors who are not pieces of the central conspiracy.

Resolving Hessa should not produce a secret order, sample shipment, or research trail that points to Maren Isle. The next chapter begins because the poisoned Storen River becomes impossible to ignore.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Valen Cemetery has been deteriorating in the background for several chapters. Reports should escalate from disturbed graves, to wandering dead, to disappearances, to organized undead activity. Do not double monster counts by calendar math. Instead, advance the {@b Cemetery Threat} one step whenever the party completes a major chapter while ignoring the problem.

entries.name: Cemetery Threat

items: {@b Restless:} isolated {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} appear near the outer wall.
{@b Predatory:} {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls} and {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters} begin hunting after dark.
{@b Organized:} {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights} direct lesser undead and abduct victims.
{@b Crisis:} the controlling vampire or equivalent undead spellcaster begins sending forces beyond the cemetery.

entries: When the party finally acts, use the current threat step to add one complication, not to multiply every encounter.

entries.name: Entering Valen Cemetery
entries: The iron gates have burst outward. Withered vegetation, overturned stones, and several mausoleums divide the cemetery into distinct zones. Supernatural clouds dim the light once the party crosses the boundary, but ordinary and magical light function normally unless a specific creature says otherwise.

entries.name: Zone A — The Poor Graves
entries: The outer graves contain newly animated {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and signs that bodies have been removed from older plots. A large crypt houses the first control focus: a bound {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} maintaining the animation. Breaking its funerary sigil, laying the spirit to rest, or defeating it stops new skeletons from rising.

entries.name: Zone B — The Marble Tower
entries: A ruined white tower contains {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} and one stronger guardian such as a {@creature Wight|XMM}. The encounter objective is to reach the upper chamber and destroy a necromantic vessel before the dead overwhelm the stair. The vessel can be smashed, consecrated, or disabled with appropriate magic.

entries.name: Zone C — The Old Crypts
entries: This quarter is hunted by {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls}, {@b Ghasts}, and one {@creature Wight|XMM} commander. Prisoners taken from Bellweather are being held here for later transformation. Rescuing them is more important than clearing every crypt.

A sealed defender's tomb contains a curated cache: one rare defensive item, one uncommon weapon or shield suited to the party, and a {@item Ring of Fire Resistance} if it fits the adventure's treasure budget.

entries.name: Zone D — Memorial Court
entries: Statues and family vaults create a maze of cover. Several spirits here are not hostile; they can explain that the undead outbreaks are being directed from deeper in the cemetery. Respectful characters can receive the location of a hidden route into the inner mausoleum.

entries.name: Zone E — The Broken Chapel
entries: The chapel has been desecrated and converted into a staging point. Use a mixed encounter of {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights}, {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters}, and lesser undead appropriate to the party. Restoring the altar weakens the inner controller by removing one environmental effect from the finale.

entries.name: Zone F — Ossuary
entries: A collapsed ossuary is filled with unstable bone piles and narrow passages. Run this as an exploration hazard with one undead ambush at most. Recoverable names and burial records help Bellweather identify victims afterward.

entries.name: Zone G — The Generating Crypt
entries: A second necromantic focus continually reanimates nearby corpses. Characters can destroy the focus, reverse its runes, or use divine magic to consecrate it. Success prevents reinforcements during the finale.

entries.name: Zone H — False Tomb
entries: The apparent resting place of the controlling undead is a decoy containing staged evidence. Careful inspection automatically reveals inconsistencies if the characters spend ten minutes comparing it with clues from Marren Library or local clergy. Do not require a single check to avoid the false conclusion.

entries.name: Zone I — Inner Mausoleum
entries: The real controller retreats here: use a {@creature Vampire|XMM}, {@creature Vampire Spawn|XMM} spellcaster, or another undead leader appropriate to the party's level. The creature's goal is survival and continued control, not a static slugfest. It uses secret passages, dominated servants, and surviving necromantic focuses to shape the fight.

entries.name: Zone J — Resting Chamber
entries: The true resting chamber contains evidence connecting the undead crisis to Tyren's broader network, but the vampire is not necessarily Tyren's servant by ideology; it may simply be exploiting the same instability. This keeps the world from collapsing into one conspiracy.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The cemetery is reclaimed when the controller is destroyed or permanently driven out and the necromantic focuses are disabled. Bellweather then holds public funerals, reburies identified dead, and creates a memorial rather than treating the site as another cleared dungeon.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Missing
entries: Families report that grave tenders and mourners have disappeared over several nights.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Bishop Brann asks the party to recover the missing if possible and stop whoever is using the cemetery.
Witnesses describe undead moving in groups toward the oldest crypts instead of wandering randomly.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The pattern suggests deliberate command.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A rescued victim can later identify the necromancer’s servants.

entries.name: Scene 2: Poor Graves
entries: The newest graves have been disturbed first because they are easiest to reach.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Tracks lead from opened graves toward an old service tunnel.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 6 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}. They are being used as labor and do not pursue far if bypassed.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Several bodies were removed without being animated, suggesting someone needs corpses elsewhere.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Re-consecrating or reburying the disturbed graves improves public trust.

entries.name: Scene 3: Marble Tower
entries: An old funerary tower serves as a lookout and holding point for captives.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Two missing grave tenders are alive inside. A signal lantern in the upper room can warn the crypts.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 2 {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A list identifies bodies with unusual magical exposure—survivors of old Radiant Well incidents are specifically marked.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Preventing the signal gives advantage on the party’s first initiative check in the crypts.

entries.name: Scene 4: Old Crypts
entries: The controlling necromancer is using Tyren’s orders to identify corpses that might serve as suitable hosts or test subjects.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The ritual chamber includes a command focus. Destroying or disabling it causes lesser undead in the crypts to stop coordinating.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Necromancer Hessa Vale is ambitious and terrified of Tyren. She bargains with information if defeat is clear.

{@b NPC description — Hessa Vale.} A severe human woman in her forties, tall and spare, with black hair streaked prematurely white and a sleepless cast to her face. She wears dark work robes under a stained leather apron, and her pale fingers are marked by ink, grave soil, and alchemical burns. Her confidence is sharp until Tyren is mentioned; then her attention becomes guarded and calculating.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use {@creature Hessa Vale|NCFA}, 1 {@creature Wight|XMM}, and 4 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Hessa's records concern her own undead experiments, grave robbing, and efforts to exploit Bellweather's instability. They do not connect her to Tyren or Yaren. Any references to bodies, souls, or suitable vessels belong to her own necromantic work rather than a shared conspiracy.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If Hessa escapes, her abandoned records still expose enough of her cemetery operation to resolve this chapter. The Maren Isle lead arrives separately through the poisoned-river crisis.

entries.name: Scene 5: Restoring the Cemetery
entries: The cemetery is a civic place of grief as much as a battlefield.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Let the party decide how much of the disturbing truth to tell families. Bishop Brann favors honesty without unnecessary detail.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 12 if using milestones. Maren Isle becomes the next urgent lead because the Storen River is beginning to sicken people.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 14
entries: After the cemetery crisis is resolved, reports of worsening contamination in the Storen River become independently urgent. Following the poisoned water leads toward Maren Isle; Hessa's records are not required and do not connect her to Yaren.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Bellweather and the cemetery’s religious interests provide {@b 6,000 gp total} for ending the disappearances, breaking the necromantic operation, and restoring the grounds. Funerary valuables remain with the dead or are returned to custodians and do not add to this total. Also award one rare defensive item (default {@b Cloak of Protection}), one uncommon weapon or shield, and a Ring of Fire Resistance if it fits the party’s needs.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 750–1,250 gp in lawful recoverable valuables, temple reward, and unclaimed treasure. Identifiable grave goods remain subject to the ownership rules in Appendix B.
{@b Consumables.} 2 healing or restorative consumables and 1 spell scroll.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item tied to burial, protection, radiant power, or the undead.
{@b Story reward.} A sanctified cemetery and lasting goodwill from clergy and affected families.

data.name: Chapter 14: Maren Isle
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 12–13

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/maren_isle.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/maren_isle.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Stop the Storen River contamination, rescue experimental captives, and gain independent evidence about Radiant Well phenomena.
The Storen River becomes contaminated, sickening residents and threatening trade. Evidence points to experiments on Maren Isle.
Stopping the contamination restores the river route and gives the party crucial information for confronting Tyren later.

With the river restored, evidence from earlier chapters and testimony from rescued regional prisoners make clear that Bellweather needs allies and safe routes before the final confrontation. Reedscale survivors can provide one supporting regional connection, but Yaren's research does not reveal Tyren's political network.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Reach the source, disable or redirect magical systems, survive defenders.
{@b Player agency.} Seek expert advice, approach by water/air, negotiate with inhabitants, or force entry.
{@b Fail forward.} The contamination’s mechanism can be understood through multiple environmental clues.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Table-Ready Purpose
entries: This is a high-magic expedition. Favor {@b Elementals}, {@b Invisible Stalkers}, {@b Gargoyles}, {@b Helmed Horrors}, and mage-type NPCs. The island should reveal who or what poisoned the river and provide a major step toward confronting Tyren.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use spellcaster stat blocks such as {@creature Mage|XMM}, {@creature Archmage|XMM} (only when level-appropriate), {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}, and magical guardians such as {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM}, {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}, or elementals. Keep the pyramid/island exploration structure.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Independent Threat: Yaren
entries: Yaren is an independent arcane opportunist, not Tyren's lieutenant and not Hessa's partner. He is attempting to reproduce Radiant Well phenomena for his own purposes.

His research can teach the party useful mechanics about consciousness, host compatibility, and interrupting transference, but it never identifies Soren as Tyren's host. That identity is reserved for the late-campaign reveal.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Storen River is being poisoned at its source by {@b Yaren}, an arcane experimenter operating from a pyramid on Maren Isle. The Council wants the contamination stopped because it blocks trade, sickens nearby districts, and prevents safe access toward Varen Keep.

entries.name: Following the River
entries: Residents, boat crews, healers, and regional travelers all provide overlapping information: the water is cleaner upstream until it reaches the island, the contamination resists ordinary purification, and strange lights are sometimes visible above the pyramid. These facts are automatic once the party asks around; checks reveal shortcuts, safe landing points, or details about Yaren's supply network.

entries.name: Reaching Maren Isle
entries: The southern water is saturated with alchemical waste. A creature that enters or drinks it makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking {@b 4d6 Poison damage} and gaining the {@b Poisoned} condition for 1 hour on a failure, or half damage with no condition on a success. Repeated exposure in the same hour increases the DC by 2.
Altered aquatic predators live near the discharge. Foreshadow them with wakes, dead fish, and movement under the surface rather than rolling random attacks every turn.
The pyramid has no obvious doors. Worn paths reveal concealed entrances on the north and south faces.

entries.name: Lower Level — The Maze
entries: Yaren uses the lower level to contain captives and failed recruits. The maze should feel tense without becoming a random-combat grinder.

{@b Prisoners.} A handful of survivors from different communities are trapped here. Hunger and fear make them cautious, not automatically hostile. Patient characters can gain information, temporary allies, and testimony against Yaren.

{@b The Keeper.} An elderly {@creature Priest|XMM} has survived by creating food and water and tending the others. He has been slowly weakening one exterior wall and can show the party a potential emergency exit.
{@b Second Maze.} Hardier prisoners and one or two dangerous altered creatures occupy this section. Use no more than one meaningful combat unless the party deliberately escalates.

{@b The Dead Writer.} A corpse hides a journal containing a rough map, a marked teleporter, and incomplete notes about Yaren's experiments. This is an automatic clue to the pyramid's internal movement system.

entries.name: Middle Level — Laboratories
entries: {@b Reedscale Cell.} Five Reedscale prisoners initially distrust anyone entering from Yaren's complex. Visible efforts to free captives, remove shackles, or share information establish good faith without a Persuasion check.
{@b Surgery.} Restraints, alchemical instruments, and recent blood make the purpose of the room clear. Keep descriptions within the table's agreed body-horror limits.

{@b Recovery Ward.} Several altered captives are in pain and frightened. They are victims, not monsters by default. Use a creature stat block only if someone panics, is magically compelled, or the party attacks first.

{@b Mixing Room.} Formulae and reports explain that Yaren is combining local water, extraplanar residue, and living subjects in an attempt to reproduce the Radiant Well's effects. The party can recover evidence, ingredients, and one useful counteragent here.

{@b Secret Stores.} Hidden chambers contain curated salvage worth about {@b 2,000 gp} in hostile-faction coin, alchemical materials, and useful equipment, plus two consumable magic items and at most one uncommon permanent item appropriate to the party. This value is part of the chapter’s 8,000 gp target.

entries.name: Upper Level — Control Rooms
entries: {@b Guard Post.} One heavily altered captive has been conditioned to attack anyone who passes without a spoken greeting. Scratched words near the threshold and repeated “hello” marks on the wall reveal the trigger. The party can speak the greeting, calm the captive, disable the door, or fight if necessary.

{@b Fountain Chamber.} Pumps force black contaminant into the river. The machinery has three visible pressure nodes. Characters can shut the system down safely with three successful actions using Arcana, Investigation, thieves' tools, smith's tools, or brute force. On a failed attempt, pressure rises and creates an environmental complication; it never explodes without warning. Once two nodes are disabled, an obvious escalating whine gives everyone one round to retreat before any major rupture.

{@b Yaren's Apartment.} Yaren is a {@creature Mage|XMM} or another arcane NPC appropriate to the party's tier. He wants specimens and research, not martyrdom. He bargains if cornered, uses control magic before lethal magic, and attempts to escape through the teleport pad or exterior route when defeat becomes likely.

{@b Pumping Room.} Three Reedscale prisoners are shackled to the pumping apparatus. They recoil from anyone wearing Yaren's insignia but stop resisting the moment characters begin freeing them. They know Yaren's routines, the teleport sequence, the location of other captives, and the hidden exit.

entries.name: Yaren's Independent Research
entries: Yaren is not Tyren's lieutenant. He is an opportunist attempting to imitate phenomena he only partly understands. His notes nevertheless provide another independent clue that the Radiant Well can alter or admit consciousness. This preserves thematic connection without making every villain part of one organization.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: Stopping the pumps and securing the research cleans the river over the following days. Bellweather's trade, sanitation, and access to the eastern ruins improve dramatically. If the Reedscale prisoners are rescued, their community becomes a minor regional ally in Chapter 15: they can provide guides, river intelligence, safe passage, and oral lore about the Radiant Well. Reedscale support does not count as one of the three strong alliances required to finish the regional arc, but it can satisfy the safe-route requirement if the party uses their river knowledge.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Poisoned River
entries: People along the Storen River report dead fish, skin burns, and magical discoloration in the water.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Sampling the water shows the contamination increases upstream toward Maren Isle.
The party can arrange a boat, use magic, or approach from the far bank.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The contamination is magical runoff, not disease. Protection from poison helps against exposure but does not clean the river.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Every day of delay worsens shortages in Bellweather but does not automatically kill named NPCs.

entries.name: Scene 2: Landing
entries: The island’s lower structures are protected by constructs and altered wildlife.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A submerged intake tunnel offers a covert route. The dock is faster but watched.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: At the dock, use 2 {@creature Animated Armor|XMM} and 2 {@creature Water Weird|XMM|Water Weirds}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Crates bear marks from river settlements, apothecaries, and alchemical suppliers, showing that Yaren collected specimens and materials through his own network rather than through Hessa's cemetery operation.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A quiet landing prevents laboratory staff from destroying research.

entries.name: Scene 3: Lower Maze
entries: The lower level channels water through unstable magical systems.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters can shut three valves to reduce hazards above. Each valve is guarded by environmental effects rather than mandatory combat: scalding steam, arcane surges, or flooding.
DC 14–16 appropriate checks or spells disable each safely.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The systems concentrate energy from old Radiant Well residue carried through subterranean channels.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: For each valve disabled, remove one lair-style hazard from the final laboratory fight.

entries.name: Scene 4: Laboratories
entries: Living captives and magical test subjects are kept here.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Rescue captives before pursuing Yaren if the party wants all survivors safe.

One chamber contains notes comparing how living and undead tissues react to Radiant-Well-like energy. The notes discuss host compatibility in abstract terms but identify no current host and no dragon.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Chief researcher Yaren is brilliant, contemptuous, and more interested in surviving with his notes than dying for his research.

{@b NPC description — Yaren.} A tall, thin high elf man of indeterminate adult age, meticulously groomed, with silver-blond hair, pale gold eyes, layered laboratory robes, and protective lenses perched above one eye. His fingers are stained by reagents. He speaks to strangers as though they are interruptions to an experiment and keeps edging toward notes, controls, or an escape route whenever the conversation turns against him.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use {@creature Yaren|NCFA}, 2 {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, and 1 {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Yaren's notes independently show that Radiant-Well-like energy can carry, admit, or displace consciousness. He theorizes that a sufficiently powerful intelligence might transfer between hosts, but he does not know Tyren's current host or the identity of that host.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing Yaren provides a technical explanation of how to interrupt transference. Killing him leaves the notes.

entries.name: Scene 5: Control Rooms
entries: The upper controls govern discharge into the river and contain the best data on Yaren's experiments with Radiant-Well-like energy and consciousness transfer.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party must shut down the discharge without causing an arcane rupture. Require three successful DC 15 Arcana, Investigation, or tool checks before two failures; appropriate spells can substitute.
On a failure, each creature in the room takes 2d6 force damage. The system still can be shut down.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Tyren can leave a host when control breaks if another viable host is nearby. The notes recommend isolating potential hosts during any confrontation.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Stopping the discharge restores the river over several days.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 15
entries: With the river restored, evidence from earlier chapters and testimony from rescued regional prisoners make clear that Bellweather needs allies and safe routes before the final confrontation. Reedscale survivors can provide one supporting regional connection, but Yaren's research does not reveal Tyren's political network.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Shutting down the laboratories and returning the research earns {@b 6,000 gp} from Bellweather and interested scholars. Place another {@b 2,000 gp} in hostile-faction coin, alchemical materials, and legitimate salvage for a chapter monetary target of about {@b 8,000 gp}. Also award 2 consumables and one uncommon permanent item (default {@b Periapt of Proof against Poison}; otherwise {@b Cloak of the Manta Ray}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character baseline. Named story relics remain in place; where an older generic treasure quantity conflicts with this section, use this section.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} About 500 gp in cash and valuables plus about 500 gp of useful alchemical or research salvage.
{@b Consumables.} 2–3 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare item, or a very rare item if the party is on curve and the item is an appropriate major chapter reward.
{@b Story reward.} A cleaner river route and the possibility of a Reedscale alliance.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Build regional leverage through alliances and selective military action rather than treating every settlement as a dungeon.
Bellweather’s survival now depends on routes and communities outside the city. The party travels beyond the ruins to build alliances before Tyren can isolate Bellweather.
The chapter ends when the party has enough regional allies, safe routes, and intelligence to survive the political crisis that follows Perrin’s betrayal.
{@b Leads onward.} Once the party has enough allies and routes, Perrin Cardon presents a supposedly urgent mission to Zennar Outpost. His betrayal begins the final political crisis.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Secure routes, negotiate alliances, neutralize genuinely hostile warbands, protect communities.
{@b Player agency.} Every settlement/stronghold should offer at least one noncombat path unless its leadership has already chosen immediate violence.
{@b Fail forward.} Diplomatic setbacks change terms and alliances; they do not force extermination.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Current Faction Rule
entries: These communities are not enemy biomes organized by species. Each location is a political or social group with its own leadership, interests, and internal disagreements. Some remain primarily one species because they are kinship communities; others are mixed. The party can negotiate, ally, trade, intimidate, infiltrate, or fight depending on what the faction is actually doing.
{@b Recommended level:} 13–15

entries.name: Table-Ready Use
entries: These wilderness sites are optional alliances, threats, and resources—not a mandatory checklist. Choose the sites that matter to the party's strategy. Currentize each community with current stat blocks and give intelligent factions goals beyond "fight the party."

These wilderness episodes are grouped together here so the adventure can use them as a regional arc rather than interrupting the city chapters at random. Not every group encountered outside Bellweather is an enemy. The party should be able to create alliances, negotiate passage, or exploit rivalries. Use the source lairs and maps while applying current encounter math.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Doman and Commander Haren Vell
entries: {@b Doman} is the deceptive mage inspired by the source adventure's manipulative spellcaster. He wants the sealed planar vessel in Iron Banner Fort and tries to persuade the party to retrieve it for him. He is not the fort commander and is not loyal to Tyren.

{@b Commander Haren Vell} commands Iron Banner Fort. Haren's relationship with Tyren is political and logistical: Tyren offers supplies, authority, and protection in exchange for obedience. Keep Doman's personal artifact scheme separate from Haren's command structure.

entries.name: Reedscale Support
entries: If the party rescued the Reedscale prisoners on Maren Isle, their community automatically becomes a minor ally. Reedscale guides can secure a river route, identify dangerous Radiant Well residue, and pass along oral history about old regional disturbances.

Reedscale support does {@b not} count as one of the three strong alliances required to finish this chapter. It can, however, satisfy the separate safe-route requirement if the party accepts and preserves the river route they offer.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: First Councilor
entries: During the regional crisis, Perrin converts his wealth, committee authority, merchant support, and administrative network into formal leadership. Unless the party has already produced extraordinary evidence sufficient to remove him from office, he becomes Bellweather's {@b First Councilor}, the formal head of the Council, before the Zennar mission.

The appointment may be contested if the party has opposed him, but it is procedurally valid. This position gives him the real seals, staff access, emergency channels, and public platform he later abuses.

entries.name: Regional Encounter Notes
entries: Currentize by biome. Favor {@creature Owlbear|XMM}, {@creature Ankheg|XMM}, {@creature Displacer Beast|XMM}, {@creature Ettercap|XMM}, {@creature Troll|XMM}, {@creature Manticore|XMM}, {@creature Bulette|XMM}, {@creature Wyvern|XMM}, {@creature Giant Crocodile|XMM}, {@creature Shambling Mound|XMM}, {@creature Will-o'-Wisp|XMM}, and culturally appropriate humanoid groups. Use reaction and morale; not every encounter is automatically hostile.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/kerren_settlement.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/kerren_settlement.webp}

Kerren is a thri-kreen settlement built among low earthen mounds and connected underground chambers. It is {@b not a treasure dungeon}. The residents are wary because armed outsiders have repeatedly entered their territory looking for relics and valuables.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Kerren sits along a route used by Tyren's couriers. The party may seek intelligence, safe passage, or help identifying troop movements.

{@b First contact.} Communication can happen through magic, gesture, a knowledgeable guide, or patient observation. Good-faith trade and respect for burial sites improve the encounter; theft or desecration turns the settlement hostile.

{@b If combat occurs.} Use current {@creature Thri-kreen|XMM|Thri-kreen} stat blocks appropriate to the party's tier. They use mobility, cover, and withdrawal rather than standing in place until killed.
{@b Reward.} Trusted characters receive regional intelligence, safe passage, supplies, and one uncommon consumable or crafted item. Sacred objects remain with the community.

{@b Bellweather consequence.} A peaceful agreement opens a safer inland route and improves Neighborhoods & Workers reputation. Violence closes that route and gives Tyren's agents an easier propaganda victory.

entries.name: Waylen Camp
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/waylen_camp.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/waylen_camp.webp}

Waylen Camp belongs to a mobile mixed-species community of herders, guides, hunters, and traders. They have no interest in conquering Bellweather and are suspicious of anyone who assumes neutrality means weakness.
{@b Why the party comes here.} The camp has seen troop columns and can identify which factions are moving under Tyren's orders. It also controls access to a reliable route through the grasslands.
{@b Finding the camp.} The party finds an abandoned campsite and fresh tracks pointing toward the current location. No random roll is required if the characters are actually searching the area.

{@b Negotiation.} The camp values useful information, medical aid, fair trade, and proof that Bellweather intends to respect local autonomy. An unprovoked attack destroys this goodwill; defenders hold the perimeter while noncombatants withdraw, and leaders seek a way to end the violence once the immediate threat is contained.
{@b Reward.} Guides, mounts, regional intelligence, and a standing invitation to trade.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} An alliance makes Bellweather less dependent on old merchant families for overland commerce, which quietly threatens Cardon's interests.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/rellan_enclave.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/rellan_enclave.webp}

Rellan is a lizardfolk enclave built around a ruined keep and flooded tunnels. The enclave is a community, not an automatically hostile monster lair. If the party rescued lizardfolk prisoners on Maren Isle, they are recognized as allies before weapons are drawn.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Rellan's elders know regional history that Bellweather's records have lost, including stories connected to the Radiant Well and the poisoned waterways.

{@b Approach.} Characters who arrive openly can request an audience. Characters sneaking into the enclave may be challenged by scouts and giant-lizard handlers, but defenders attempt to identify intruders before escalating to lethal force.

{@b Terrain.} Collapsed masonry and flooded tunnels create {@b Difficult Terrain}. Underwater passages connect several pools; a 10-minute search finds them automatically, while a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check spots them immediately. Use normal 2024 underwater-combat rules.
{@b If combat occurs.} Use current {@b Lizardfolk} and {@b Giant Lizard} stat blocks. Defenders retreat through the water routes when badly outmatched.

{@b Reward.} Allies are welcomed to a feast and receive safe passage, regional lore, and a bronze friendship token recognized by allied communities. Exceptional service can earn one uncommon consumable or crafted weapon.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} Peaceful relations establish a southern ally and challenge the idea that every group outside Bellweather must be conquered or absorbed.

entries.name: Ash Road Warband
entries: The Ash Road Warband is a {@b named hostile faction}, not a stand-in for all orcs. Its members raid settlements, take captives, and serve Tyren because the arrangement gives their leaders weapons, territory, and protection. The force itself can include multiple species.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Refugees report kidnappings and burned caravans. Scouts also connect the warband to Tyren's courier network.

{@b Approach.} The party finds signs of violence before reaching the camp: burned wagons, frightened survivors, and scouts watching the road. A wounded survivor can identify the direction captives were taken; their fate depends on the party's aid rather than a scripted death.

{@b Encounter structure.} Do not run dozens of low-level attackers. Use 6–10 meaningful combatants, a leader, one specialist, and an objective such as opening the captive pen, disabling a signal horn, or preventing a courier from escaping.
{@b Captives.} If the warband threatens prisoners, that creates a rescue clock. Refusing to intervene is a story and reputation consequence, never an alignment punishment.

{@b Treasure.} The war chest contains {@b 4,000 gp} in coin and trade bars, three art objects included within the regional treasure budget, two consumable magic items, and one rare level-appropriate permanent item.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} Rescued captives bring testimony about Tyren's logistics. How Bellweather treats surrendered warband members becomes a visible test of the city's values.

entries.name: Emmer Hold
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/emmer_hold.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/emmer_hold.webp}

Emmer Hold is a fortified kobold-majority settlement built into old mining works and drainage tunnels. It is {@b not a dungeon full of creatures who exist to be cleared}. Most residents are miners, craftspeople, families, traders, and laborers. A militant faction inside the hold has accepted arms and promises from Tyren's agents in exchange for harassing Bellweather's roads.

entries.name: Why the Party Comes Here
entries: Choose whichever hook follows from play:

items: caravans report disciplined ambushes using Emmer-made traps;
the Council wants safe passage through the nearby road;
a Bellweather merchant claims the entire mine under an old deed, creating a dispute before the party ever arrives;
Emmer dissidents quietly ask for help removing the Tyren-aligned commander.

entries.name: The Situation
entries: {@b Kessa Ember}, a practical kobold engineer, speaks for residents who want neutrality and trade. {@creature Daren Voss|NCFA}, a mixed-species mercenary captain using the Warrior Veteran stat block, commands the Tyren-aligned fighters. The militant force consists of {@b Kobold Warriors, Guards, Scouts,} and a small number of specialists; do not deploy mass waves.

The party can resolve Emmer Hold by negotiation, exposing Daren's arrangement with Tyren, defeating his command cell, sabotaging the weapons cache, or convincing residents that Bellweather will recognize their right to remain. A direct assault is possible but immediately damages Independent Factions reputation and turns civilians into evacuees rather than combatants.

items: {@b Outer Works.} Traps, warning bells, and observation points. The challenge is getting close without convincing the whole settlement it is under invasion.
{@b Commons.} Civilian heart of the hold. Violence here has severe political consequences.
{@b Forge Gallery.} Evidence that outside agents supplied military-grade material.
{@b Command Chamber.} Daren and 2–4 elite allies. Use terrain, cover, and a surrender threshold rather than a fight to the death.
{@b Old Treasury.} Most wealth is communal reserve, payroll, and trade stock. The party's actual reward is a curated cache: coin, consumables, and at most one level-appropriate permanent item.

entries.name: Bellweather Consequence
entries: A negotiated settlement can open a new trade route and add kobold engineers to Bellweather reconstruction projects. A conquest secures the road faster but creates refugees, resentment, and a visible test of what “reclamation” means when another community already lives there.

entries.name: Iron Banner Fort
entries: The Iron Banner is a disciplined military faction headquartered in a fortified hill complex. Its core leadership is hobgoblin, but its ranks include several species bound by pay, oath, coercion, family ties, or belief that Tyren offers stability. The fort is a {@b military and civilian settlement}, not an ancestry-coded extermination dungeon.

items: Iron Banner patrols are closing a road Bellweather needs.
Prisoners taken from a caravan are being held for leverage.
A dissident officer offers intelligence in exchange for safe passage.

{@creature Doman|NCFA}, a deceptive spellcaster seeking an artifact in the fort, tries to manipulate the party into doing his work. Use his NCFA stat block and let the party expose or refuse him without losing access to the adventure.

entries.name: Faction Structure
entries: {@creature Commander Haren Vell|NCFA} uses the Gladiator stat block. He is loyal to Tyren because Tyren guarantees supplies and regional authority. {@creature Captain Sera Dorn|NCFA} uses the Warrior Veteran stat block and is willing to negotiate if the party can prove Tyren is treating the Iron Banner as disposable. The fort also contains guards, scouts, smiths, healers, families, prisoners, and noncombatant workers.

entries.name: Running the Fort
entries: Treat the fort as five zones rather than thirty rooms of attrition:

items: {@b Outer Patrol Line.} A reconnaissance, stealth, diplomacy, or short skirmish scene. Do not use 25–50 creature waves.
{@b Barracks and Works.} The party can sabotage supplies, free prisoners, gather evidence, or win over soldiers.
{@b Civilian Quarter.} No combat objective requires harming civilians. Their presence is explicit so players understand the faction is a society, not a monster nest.

{@b Temple and Command Hall.} Religious and political leadership can be separated from rank-and-file soldiers. Coercive priests use {@b Cult Fanatic/Priest} style stat blocks; soldiers use current martial NPCs.
{@b Command Vault.} The climactic confrontation centers on Commander Haren, 2–4 elite allies, and an objective such as seizing orders, stopping a signal, or preventing destruction of evidence.

entries.name: Doman's Artifact
entries: The source adventure places an unusually powerful magic cache here. In this adventure, the object Doman wants is a {@b sealed planar vessel} connected to research on the Radiant Well. It is valuable because of what it proves, not because it grants a pile of unrelated powers. If the party keeps it, it functions primarily as a story key until the DM chooses an appropriate level-15 reward.

entries.name: Outcomes
entries: {@b Alliance or armistice:} The Iron Banner withdraws support from Tyren, Independent Factions reputation rises, and Bellweather gains a disciplined neighboring power rather than conquered territory.
{@b Leadership defeat:} The faction fractures; some soldiers surrender or leave, while civilians remain. Bellweather must decide whether to recognize local self-government.
{@b Total assault:} Militarily possible, but costly. Independent Factions reputation falls and Perrin can exploit the bloodshed politically.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Do not award the source module's enormous coin piles and stacks of +1/+2/+3 gear. The fort's wealth is payroll, communal stores, equipment, and regional trade stock. A successful resolution grants a level-appropriate monetary reward, 2–3 consumables, and at most one permanent rare/very rare item that fits the party and current tier.

entries.name: Chapter Structure
entries: This chapter is a regional alliance arc. The party does not need every community as an ally. Three strong alliances plus a safe route are enough to move forward. Each location should feel like a community with its own interests, not a monster encounter with a settlement attached.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement: The Water Dispute
entries: Kerren is divided over access to a spring after armed outsiders begin taxing travelers.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can expose the outsiders’ connection to Tyren, negotiate a shared water schedule, or drive off the extortionists.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Elder Sella Kerren, a thri-kreen elder, wants stability and hates being treated as a subordinate of Bellweather.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If fighting occurs, use 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} and 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The extortionists carry Storen Gate-era command marks and promises of future authority under Tyren.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Resolve the water dispute fairly and Kerren provides scouts and food.

entries.name: Waylen Camp: The Missing Hunters
entries: Several hunters disappeared after following tracks into old ruins near the camp.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party locates the missing hunters and finds them trapped by a predator rather than enemy soldiers.
Returning them alive matters more than killing the creature.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Waylen’s leader, Jorn Waylen, a human man, is suspicious of city promises but respects people who show up when help is needed.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Bulette|XMM}. It attacks from below and retreats if badly injured.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The hunters saw Tyren-aligned couriers avoiding Waylen territory by taking the Ash Road.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Waylen provides guides and a hidden route if helped.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave: The Internal Split
entries: Rellan’s residents are divided between neutrality and alliance with Bellweather.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A Tyren-aligned agent is paying agitators to sabotage talks. The party can identify the payments, protect a public meeting, and expose the agent.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Speaker Mara Rellan, a lizardfolk woman, wants proof before taking sides. Young militants want immediate alliance; merchants fear retaliation.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If exposed, the agent uses {@creature Assassin|XMM} and tries to escape rather than fight to the death.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Payment records tie the agent directly to the Ash Road Warband.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Exposing manipulation earns Rellan’s political support and messengers.

entries.name: Ash Road Warband: Break the Command
entries: Unlike the communities, the Ash Road Warband actively raids for Tyren.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can attack the camp, challenge leadership, or turn disaffected members against the commanders.
Targeting food stores or mounts can end the warband’s ability to raid without killing everyone.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: War leader Kesh serves Tyren for promised land and rank. Several lieutenants doubt those promises.

{@b NPC description — War Leader Kesh.} A tall orc man in early middle age, massively built and battle-scarred, with one broken lower tusk, a heavy cloak, and trophies taken only from defeated enemy officers rather than civilians. His voice is trained to carry over a battlefield. Kesh projects certainty in public, but watches lieutenants closely whenever Tyren's promises are questioned.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Gladiator|XMM}, 2 {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, and 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} for the command group.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
